definition_zh: 迅速的；及时的；准时的；促使；提示；提示符
definition_en: quick and without delay, done at the agreed time, to cause someone to act, or a cue that helps someone carry on
core_image: 有人在旁边轻轻敲一下桌面，另一个人立刻抬头，手上的动作马上跟上来
scene: 排练到一半，演员忘了下一句，场边的人压低声音把词递过去，演员立刻接上。A stagehand prompted him from the wings, and the scene moved on.
sceneCN: 这里表示「提词、提示」（第 4 个义项：把对方要说的话小声递过去）；句意为舞台工作人员在侧幕给他提词，戏便接着演下去。

pos.zh: 迅速的；及时的；准时的
促使；提示；提词
提示；提词；提示符

derivatives.zh: 由 prompt 加 -ly 构成，义为「迅速地；准时地」
由 prompt 加 -ness 构成，义为「迅速；及时」
由 prompt 加 -ing 构成，义为「提示；鼓励」
由 prompt 加 -er 构成，义为「提词员；提词器」

senses.title: Done quickly and without delay
senses.definition: acting or happening quickly, with no waiting in between
senses.definitionCN: 动作或事情发生得快，中间没有等待
senses.example: We received a prompt answer to our letter.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的信很快得到了答复。
senses.why: The Latin participle described something already brought out and therefore lying within reach, and what lies within reach can be used at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词描述的是已经被拿出来、因此就在手边的东西；就在手边的东西，随时都能用上。

senses.title: Arriving exactly at the agreed time
senses.definition: arriving or happening exactly at the stated time, neither early nor late
senses.definitionCN: 在约定的时刻到达或发生，不早也不晚
senses.example: Please be prompt for the eight o'clock train.
senses.exampleCN: 请准时赶上八点的火车。
senses.why: If readiness is the core, the clearest proof of readiness is being already there when the clock strikes, so the word takes on the sense of punctuality.
senses.whyCN: 如果核心是「随时可用」，那么最清楚的证明就是钟声一响人已经到位，于是这个词带上了「守时」的意思。

senses.title: To cause someone to do something
senses.definition: to make a person decide to do something, usually by something seen, heard or felt
senses.definitionCN: 通常因看到、听到或感到某事而使人决定去做
senses.example: The smell of smoke prompted him to check the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 烟味促使他去厨房查看。
senses.why: The verb first meant to bring words out of someone; from bringing out words it widened to bringing out any action at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最初指把话从别人嘴里引出来；从「引出话」扩大到「引出任何行动」。

senses.title: To supply the next words to a speaker
senses.definition: to say the next words quietly to an actor or speaker who has forgotten them
senses.definitionCN: 小声把下一句台词说给忘词的演员或发言人
senses.example: The teacher prompted the child with the first word.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把第一个词提示给孩子。
senses.why: Theatre keeps the oldest visible sense: a helper at the side brings the forgotten line back into the actor's mouth.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧保留了最古老也最可见的那一层：助手在侧边把忘掉的台词重新送进演员嘴里。

senses.title: A cue or sign that tells you what to do next
senses.definition: a word, signal or symbol that shows a person, or a computer, what to do next
senses.definitionCN: 提示人或计算机下一步该做什么的词、信号或符号
senses.example: The program waits for a prompt before it continues.
senses.exampleCN: 程序会等一个提示符，然后才继续运行。
senses.why: A cue is still something brought out in front of you at the right moment, so the noun serves both the stage whisper and the blinking sign on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 提示仍然是在恰当的时刻被拿到你面前的东西，所以这个名词既能指舞台上的低语，也能指屏幕上闪动的记号。

intro.en: Prompt goes back to a Latin verb for taking something out; what has been brought out is ready at hand, and ready things act fast.
intro.cn: prompt 可追到拉丁语中表示「拿出来」的动词；被拿出来的东西就在手边，而在手边的东西动作就快。

items.en: Emere meant to take or to buy, the act of getting something into your hands.
items.cn: emere 意为拿取、购买，是把某物弄到手里的动作。

items.en: With pro-, the verb became promere, to bring forth or produce, as if drawing something out into the open.
items.cn: 加上 pro-，动词成为 promere，意为拿出来、取出，像是把东西从里面拿到明处。

items.en: The participle promptus described what had been brought forth, and so what was ready at hand and quick to use.
items.cn: 分词 promptus 描述已经被拿出来、因此就在手边、随时可用的东西。

items.en: Late Latin promptare meant to bring out or to suggest, and from it came the verb sense of urging someone to speak or act.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 promptare 意为拿出、提示，由它产生「催人开口或行动」的动词义。

items.en: French prompt entered English, which kept the adjective of readiness, added the verbs of urging and cueing, and later lent the noun to computing.
items.cn: 法语 prompt 进入英语，保留了「随时可用」的形容词义，加上「催促」与「提词」的动词义，后来又把名词借给了计算机领域。

note.en: The first group is the same Latin verb and the English forms built on it, including the phrase that still carries the old picture; the second group gathers words for speed and good timing.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁动词及其上的英语形式，包括仍保留旧画面的那个说法；第二组收表示快与准时的词。

entries.definition: A person or device that supplies forgotten lines.
entries.definitionCN: 提示台词的人或设备；提词员、提词器。

entries.definition: The act of cueing someone, or a nudge that makes someone act.
entries.definitionCN: 给人提示的行为，或促使人行动的一推。

entries.definition: The quality of being quick and punctual.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而准时的品质。

entries.definition: Done without preparation, literally done out of readiness.
entries.definitionCN: 即兴的、无准备的；字面义为「出自现成的状态」。

entries.definition: Moving or finishing in a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 在很短时间内移动或完成的。

entries.definition: Fast and smooth in movement, often in a literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动作又快又顺，常带文学色彩。

entries.definition: Happening at once, with nothing in between.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻发生，中间没有间隔。

entries.definition: Arriving exactly at the agreed time.
entries.definitionCN: 正好在约定的时间到达。

normalIntro.en: The whole family grows from one Latin picture: something is taken out and held ready, so it can be handed over the moment it is needed.
normalIntro.cn: 整族词都长自同一幅拉丁画面：东西被拿出来、握在手中待用，因此需要的那一刻就能递过去。

normal.en: Emere is to take, pro- is forward, so promere is to bring something out in front of you.
normal.cn: emere 是拿取，pro- 是向前，所以 promere 就是把东西拿到你面前。

normal.en: Promptus means already brought out, which explains why prompt means quick: ready things need no searching.
normal.cn: promptus 意为已经被拿出来，这就解释了 prompt 为什么是「快」：现成的东西不必再找。

normal.en: The verb sense of urging grows from the same image, because you bring words out of someone who has stopped speaking.
normal.cn: 动词「促使」也出自同一幅图：你把话从突然停住的人嘴里引出来。

normal.en: Impromptu keeps the Latin phrase in promptu, meaning in readiness, so an impromptu speech is one given straight out of what is at hand.
normal.cn: impromptu 保留了拉丁语 in promptu，意为「现成可用」，所以即兴演讲就是直接用手边现成的东西讲。

normal.en: A computer prompt is still a cue: the screen brings a question out and waits for your reply.
normal.cn: 计算机里的 prompt 仍是提示：屏幕把一个问题拿到你面前，然后等你的回答。

abstract.en: Prompt links speed to readiness, which suggests that haste here is not hurry but the absence of searching.
abstract.cn: prompt 把「快」和「现成」系在一起，说明这里的快不是慌忙，而是不必再找。

abstract.en: One word serves an actor's cue and a machine's signal, because both are a small push that keeps a process moving.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指演员的提词，也指机器的信号，因为两者都是让流程继续下去的一小推。

abstract.en: To prompt someone is to lend them the next step, and every prompt is therefore a small act of trust.
abstract.cn: 给人提示就是把下一步借给他，所以每次提示都是一次微小的信任。

examples.en: She gave a prompt reply to every question.
examples.cn: 她对每个问题都迅速作答。

examples.en: The letter prompted him to write back at once.
examples.cn: 这封信促使他立刻回信。

examples.en: The screen showed a prompt and waited.
examples.cn: 屏幕上出现一个提示，然后等着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑荣扑」——有人在背后一推，人就扑腾着动起来；记住 prompt 是迅速的、促使人。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、往外）+ emere（拿取、买）→ promere（拿出来、取出）→ promptus（已拿出来的、就在手边的）→ 晚期拉丁语 promptare（提示、催），经法语 prompt 进入英语；prompt 的「快」本义是「东西已在手边，随时可用」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is something brought out and lying ready; from it come quickness, punctuality, the act of urging, the stage whisper and the screen cue.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被拿出来、就在手边待用」；由此分出迅速、准时、促使人行动、舞台提词与屏幕提示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand already holding what will be needed, so the moment it is asked for, it is there.
core.cn: 核心意象：手里早已握着待会儿要用的东西，别人一要，立刻就在。

branches.en: a reply handed over before it is even expected
branches.cn: 答复在别人预料之前就递到

branches.en: a smell of smoke sending someone to the kitchen
branches.cn: 烟味把人赶去厨房查看

branches.en: a whisper from the wings feeding the next line
branches.cn: 侧幕的低语把下一句递上台

branches.en: a blinking sign on a screen waiting for input
branches.cn: 屏幕上闪着的记号等着输入

branches.en: haste and cue living in one word
branches.cn: 迅速与提示共用一个词

intro.en: A Latin verb of taking out, its participle, and the English endings that make adverbs and nouns from the adjective hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「拿出来」的拉丁动词、它的分词，以及把这个形容词变成副词与名词的英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Promere and its participle promptus are the reliable Latin cognates, and emere is the verb inside promere.
latinIntro.cn: promere 及其分词 promptus 是可靠的同源词，而 emere 是 promere 里面的那个动词。

items.meaningCN: 已拿出来的；随时可用的

definition_zh: 迅速地；立即；准时地；干脆地
definition_en: in a quick and immediate way, or exactly at the arranged time
core_image: 指针刚跳到约定的那一格，人已经站在门口，东西也都准备好了
scene: 邮局刚开门，柜台前的人就把一叠信递上去，说这些都得当天寄出。She answered the letter promptly and posted it the same morning.
sceneCN: 这里表示「迅速地、立即」（第 1 个义项：几乎没有拖延就做出反应）；句意为她很快回了信，并在当天上午寄了出去。

pos.zh: 迅速地；立即；准时地；干脆地

derivatives.zh: promptly 的基础词，义为「迅速的；促使」
由 prompt 加 -ness 构成，义为「迅速；及时」
由 prompt 加 -ing 构成，义为「提示；鼓励」

senses.title: Without delay; at once
senses.definition: in a way that happens at once, with almost no gap between the cause and the response
senses.definitionCN: 事情立刻发生，起因与反应之间几乎没有间隔
senses.example: The nurse answered the bell promptly.
senses.exampleCN: 护士听到铃声立刻应了。
senses.why: The adjective described something ready at hand, and -ly turns that readiness into the manner of an action: nothing has to be fetched first.
senses.whyCN: 形容词本指「就在手边、随时可用」，-ly 把这份现成变成动作的方式：不必先去取什么。

senses.title: Exactly at the agreed time
senses.definition: at the stated time and not later, so that an appointment or timetable is kept
senses.definitionCN: 在说定的时刻，不拖延，从而守住约定或时刻表
senses.example: The train left promptly at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 火车七点整开走了。
senses.why: If readiness is the point, the sharpest display of it is being in place when the clock reaches the agreed mark, which is why the adverb also means punctually.
senses.whyCN: 如果要点是「随时可用」，那么最利落的展示就是钟点一到人已到位，所以这个副词也有「准时」之意。

senses.title: Without hesitation in answering or deciding
senses.definition: in a way that shows no hesitation, especially when agreeing, refusing or admitting something
senses.definitionCN: 表现出毫不迟疑，尤指在答应、拒绝或承认某事时
senses.example: He promptly agreed to take the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 他干脆地答应上夜班。
senses.why: A ready answer is not only fast but unhedged; English lets the same adverb carry that firmness of a decision already made.
senses.whyCN: 现成的回答不仅快，而且不含糊；英语就让同一个副词承担这种「主意已定」的干脆。

intro.en: Promptly is an English-made adverb: the borrowed adjective prompt was simply given the native ending -ly, and the Latin picture of readiness came along with it.
intro.cn: promptly 是在英语内部造出的副词：借来的形容词 prompt 加上本族词尾 -ly，拉丁语「现成待用」的画面也一并跟了过来。

items.en: Emere meant to take or to buy, getting something into your hands.
items.cn: emere 意为拿取、购买，是把某物弄到手里。

items.en: Pro- plus emere gave promere, to bring something out into the open.
items.cn: pro- 加 emere 构成 promere，意为把东西拿到明处。

items.en: The participle promptus named what had been brought out, hence what is ready and quick to use.
items.cn: 分词 promptus 指已经被拿出来的东西，因此是现成、随时可用的。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective prompt from French and Latin, meaning ready and quick, and used it for both people and replies.
items.cn: 英语从法语和拉丁语借来形容词 prompt，意为现成而快速的，既用于人，也用于答复。

items.en: The native suffix -ly turned that adjective into an adverb of manner, so promptly means in a ready and immediate way.
items.cn: 本族词尾 -ly 把这个形容词变成方式副词，所以 promptly 意为「以现成、即刻的方式」。

note.en: The first group is the small English family around the adjective, including one formal noun; the second group gathers adverbs and near-synonyms of speed and timing.
note.cn: 第一组是围绕这个形容词的小词族，包括一个正式的名词；第二组收表示速度与时刻的副词及近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective and verb this adverb is built on: ready, quick, to urge.
entries.definitionCN: 这个副词所依附的形容词与动词：现成的、快的、促使。

entries.definition: The quality of being quick and punctual.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而准时的品质。

entries.definition: A formal noun for readiness and speed of action.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指行动的敏捷与果断。

entries.definition: The act of cueing someone or nudging them to act.
entries.definitionCN: 给人提示或促使人行动的行为。

entries.definition: At a fast speed, with emphasis on how short the time is.
entries.definitionCN: 以很快的速度，强调时间之短。

entries.definition: At once, with no interval at all.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻，完全没有间隔。

entries.definition: Exactly at the stated time.
entries.definitionCN: 正好在说定的时刻。

entries.definition: Fast and smoothly, often with a literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 又快又顺，常带文学色彩。

normalIntro.en: The adverb adds only a suffix to the adjective, so everything it means is the adjective's readiness turned into a way of acting.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词只在形容词上加了一个词尾，所以它的全部含义都是把形容词的「现成」变成做事的方式。

normal.en: Prompt means ready at hand; add -ly and you get the manner of acting out of that readiness.
normal.cn: prompt 意为「就在手边待用」；加上 -ly，得到的就是从这份现成里长出的做事方式。

normal.en: Promptly at nine and promptly replied share one word because both show something already in place when needed.
normal.cn: promptly at nine 与 promptly replied 共用一个词，因为两者都表现出「需要时已经就位」。

normal.en: The -ly ending is native English, so promptly was made inside English rather than borrowed whole.
normal.cn: -ly 是英语本族词尾，所以 promptly 是在英语内部造出来的，而不是整体借来的。

normal.en: Promptitude is the formal cousin of promptness, both naming the same readiness as a quality.
normal.cn: promptitude 是 promptness 的正式近亲，两者都把同一份「现成」说成一种品质。

normal.en: Because it carries no hint of hurrying, promptly can describe calm efficiency rather than panic.
normal.cn: 由于它不带慌乱之意，promptly 可以形容从容的效率，而不是手忙脚乱。

abstract.en: Promptly measures the gap between needing something and having it, and tries to make that gap vanish.
abstract.cn: promptly 衡量的是「需要」与「到手」之间的空隙，并试图让这个空隙消失。

abstract.en: The same adverb covers speed and punctuality because both are forms of not keeping anyone waiting.
abstract.cn: 同一个副词兼指快与准时，因为两者都是「不让人等」的形式。

abstract.en: A prompt reply is a courtesy in grammar as well as in manners: it treats the other person's time as real.
abstract.cn: 迅速回复既是语法上的词，也是礼节上的事：它把别人的时间当真。

examples.en: She replied promptly to every message.
examples.cn: 她对每条消息都迅速回复。

examples.en: The meeting began promptly at nine.
examples.cn: 会议九点整准时开始。

examples.en: He promptly denied the rumour.
examples.cn: 他干脆地否认了那个传言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普让普特利」——一催就动，动作快得带响；记住 promptly 是迅速地。

root: 由 prompt（迅速的；准时的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；prompt 源自拉丁语 promere（拿出来）的分词 promptus（就在手边的），所以 promptly 的核心仍是「东西已在手边，动作立刻跟上」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is acting out of readiness; the adverb then splits into speed, punctuality, and the firmness of a decision made without hedging.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「凭着现成而行动」；副词由此分出迅速、准时，以及不加含糊的果断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the clock reaching the agreed mark while the person is already at the door, everything in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟点刚到约定的那一格，人已站在门口，东西都在手上。

branches.en: a hand already raised before the question ends
branches.cn: 问题还没问完，手已经举起来

branches.en: a clock and a person arriving on the same beat
branches.cn: 钟点与人同时到位

branches.en: an answer that refuses to hedge
branches.cn: 毫不含糊的回答

branches.en: a letter written and posted in one morning
branches.cn: 同一个上午写完并寄出的信

branches.en: a quick yes given without a second thought
branches.cn: 不加犹豫就给出的答应

intro.en: The adverb is a Latin readiness carried by a French adjective and finished with a native English suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词是拉丁语的「现成」，由法语形容词承载，再用英语本族词尾收尾。

latinIntro.en: Promptus, the participle of promere, is the reliable Latin cognate behind both prompt and promptly.
latinIntro.cn: promere 的分词 promptus 是 prompt 与 promptly 背后可靠的同源词。

items.meaningCN: 已拿出来的；随时可用的

items.meaning: in a ready and quick way

definition_zh: 代词
definition_en: a word such as he, she, it or they that is used in place of a noun or a noun phrase
core_image: 一个人指着空椅子说「他」，椅子上没有人，那个名字已被一个短词顶替
scene: 介绍新同事时，老员工不愿反复念那个长名字，只用「他」来指，大家也都听得懂。The pronoun saved everyone from repeating the long name in every sentence.
sceneCN: 这里表示「代词」（第 1 个义项：用来代替名词或名词短语的词）；句意为代词让大家不必在每句话里重复那个长名字。

pos.zh: 代词

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 pronomin- 加 -al 构成，义为「代词的；起代词作用的」
由 pronominal 加 -ly 构成，义为「以代词的方式」

senses.title: A word that stands in for a noun
senses.definition: a word used instead of a noun or noun phrase, so that the same name does not have to be repeated
senses.definitionCN: 用来代替名词或名词短语的词，免得同一个名字反复出现
senses.example: In the sentence she wrote it, both she and it are pronouns.
senses.exampleCN: 在 she wrote it 这句话里，she 与 it 都是代词。
senses.why: Latin pro- means for or instead of and nomen means name, so the word is literally a stand-in for a name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pro- 意为「代替、为了」，nomen 意为「名字」，所以这个词字面上就是「名字的替身」。

senses.title: A pronoun marking who speaks, is spoken to, or is spoken about
senses.definition: a pronoun that points to the speaker, the listener, or a third person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 指说话人、听话人，或第三方的人与物的代词
senses.example: I, you, he, she, we and they are personal pronouns.
senses.exampleCN: I、you、he、she、we、they 都是人称代词。
senses.why: Grammarians sorted the class by the three roles of a conversation, so the pronouns that mark those roles received a name of their own.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家按对话的三方角色给这一类词再分类，标出这些角色的代词便单独有了名称。

senses.title: A pronoun that introduces a clause and links it to a noun
senses.definition: a pronoun such as who, which or that that opens a subordinate clause and connects it to the noun before it
senses.definitionCN: 像 who、which、that 这样引出从句并把它接到前面名词上的代词
senses.example: In the phrase the man who called, who is a relative pronoun.
senses.exampleCN: 在 the man who called 这个短语里，who 是关系代词。
senses.why: A relative pronoun still stands for the noun in front of it, yet at the same moment it opens a clause, so one short word does two jobs.
senses.whyCN: 关系代词仍然代替它前面的名词，同时又引出一个从句，于是一个短词兼做两件事。

senses.title: A pronoun that shows possession without the noun
senses.definition: a pronoun such as mine, yours or theirs that carries the idea of ownership while the noun is left out
senses.definitionCN: 像 mine、yours、theirs 这样带着归属含义、却把名词省去的代词
senses.example: Mine and theirs are possessive pronouns because each replaces a whole noun phrase.
senses.exampleCN: mine 与 theirs 是物主代词，因为它们各自代替了一整个名词短语。
senses.why: The possessive form keeps the ownership but drops the owned thing, which is exactly the substituting work a pronoun does.
senses.whyCN: 物主形式保留了归属，却省掉了被归属的东西，这正是代词「顶替」的本职。

intro.en: Pronoun is a Latin translation of a Greek grammar term: pro- for instead of, nomen for name. It names a word that occupies the place a name would take.
intro.cn: pronoun 是对一个希腊语法术语的拉丁翻译：pro- 意为代替，nomen 意为名字。它指的就是占据名字位置的词。

items.en: Nomen meant name, and it also supplied noun and a whole family of words about naming.
items.cn: nomen 意为名字，也是 noun 以及一整族与命名有关的词的来源。

items.en: Greek grammarians called the class antonymia, built from anti, instead of, and onoma, name.
items.cn: 希腊语法学家把这一类词称作 antonymia，由 anti（代替）与 onoma（名字）构成。

items.en: Latin teachers translated the Greek term piece by piece, producing pronomen, literally a word standing for a name.
items.cn: 拉丁语教师把这个希腊术语逐块翻译，造出 pronomen，字面就是「代替名字的词」。

items.en: Old French pronom carried the grammar label into English use, and the spelling later settled as pronoun.
items.cn: 古法语 pronom 把这个语法标签带进英语，拼写后来固定为 pronoun。

items.en: English keeps pronoun as the general label and names each subclass by the work it does in the sentence.
items.cn: 现代英语把 pronoun 保留为总称，再按各小类在句中的功能分别命名。

note.en: The first group collects same-root relatives plus two words that merely look alike and must not be confused; the second group collects the other word classes a pronoun is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组收同源近亲，外加两个只是长得像、必须分清的词；第二组收与代词常被放在一起比较的其他词类。

entries.definition: A word for a person, place or thing; it shares the Latin name-word but does the naming itself.
entries.definitionCN: 表示人、地或物的词；与本词共用拉丁「名字」一词，但它自己就是命名的那一方。

entries.definition: Relating to a pronoun, or behaving like one in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 与代词有关的，或在句中起代词作用的。

entries.definition: To say a word aloud; only the spelling is close, the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 把词读出声；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The way a word is spoken; it looks like this word but has nothing to do with grammar, only the spelling is close and the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 词的读法；它看起来像这个词，却与语法无关，只是拼写相近、词源不同。

entries.definition: A word for an action or a state, another word class.
entries.definitionCN: 表示动作或状态的词，属于另一词类。

entries.definition: A word that describes or limits a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰或限定名词的词；形容词。

entries.definition: A word that modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰动词、形容词或另一副词的词。

entries.definition: A word such as the or this placed before a noun to limit it.
entries.definitionCN: 像 the 或 this 那样放在名词前起限定作用的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a literal translation of a Greek grammar term, which is why its two halves still say exactly what it does: in place of a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是对一个希腊语法术语的逐字翻译，所以它的两半至今仍直接说出它的功能：站在名字的位置上。

normal.en: Pro- in Latin means for or instead of, and nomen means name, so pronomen is a word taking the place of a name.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pro- 意为「代替、为了」，nomen 意为名字，所以 pronomen 就是替名字站位的词。

normal.en: Greek grammarians said anti plus onoma; Latin teachers translated both halves, which is why the English word is so transparent.
normal.cn: 希腊语法学家说 anti 加 onoma；拉丁语教师把两半都译了出来，所以英语这个词一眼就能看懂。

normal.en: Personal pronouns divide by who is speaking, so one class is seen from three positions in the conversation.
normal.cn: 人称代词按「谁在说」来分，于是同一个词类从对话的三个位置来看。

normal.en: A relative pronoun replaces a noun and joins a clause at the same time, which is how who can do the work of two words.
normal.cn: 关系代词既代替名词又连接从句，所以 who 能做一个两词才能做的活。

normal.en: A possessive pronoun keeps the ownership but drops the noun, so mine stands for my something without naming it.
normal.cn: 物主代词保留归属、省掉名词，所以 mine 代替 my 加某物，却不必说出那是什么。

abstract.en: A pronoun is economy in grammar: it lets a language avoid saying the same name twice.
abstract.cn: 代词是语法里的节省：它让语言不必把同一个名字说两遍。

abstract.en: Every pronoun leans on something said earlier, so the class is a reminder that words can point instead of name.
abstract.cn: 每个代词都倚靠前面说过的东西，所以这个词类提醒人：词可以指，而不必命名。

abstract.en: Because a pronoun can change referent with a glance or a gesture, grammar and pointing share one small word.
abstract.cn: 由于一个眼神或手势就能改变代词的所指，语法与指点动作共用一个小词。

examples.en: Every pronoun in the paragraph refers back to the scientist.
examples.cn: 这一段里的每个代词都回指那位科学家。

examples.en: Use a pronoun instead of the full name when the meaning is clear.
examples.cn: 意思清楚时用代词代替全名。

examples.en: The pronoun they can now refer to a single person.
examples.cn: 代词 they 现在也能指单个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若诺恩」——把长名字折成一个短音，像把名字缩成影子；记住 pronoun 是代词。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（代替、为了）+ nomen（名字）→ pronomen（代替名字的词）；一般认为这是拉丁语法学家对希腊语 anti 加 onoma 的逐字翻译，经古法语 pronom 进入英语。注意它与 pronunciation（发音）只是拼写相近，来源与意义都不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a word standing where a name would stand; the personal, relative and possessive subclasses each show one kind of work that stand-in can do.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「站在名字位置上的词」；人称、关系、物主等小类，各自展示这个替身能做的一种活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing at an empty chair while a short word does the work of a long name.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指着空椅子，一个短词顶替了那个长名字。

branches.en: a long name folded into one short word
branches.cn: 长长的名字被折成一个短词

branches.en: three people in a conversation, each with a pronoun
branches.cn: 对话中的三方各有自己的代词

branches.en: a clause joined to a noun by a single word
branches.cn: 一个词把从句接到名词上

branches.en: ownership kept while the object is left out
branches.cn: 归属还在，被归属的东西却省去了

branches.en: the same stand-in doing different jobs
branches.cn: 同一个替身做着不同的活

intro.en: A Latin prefix of substitution, the Latin word for name, and the endings that make the adjective and the adverb hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示代替的拉丁前缀、拉丁语的「名字」，以及造出形容词与副词的词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Pronomen and nomen are the reliable Latin cognates; the Greek term behind them is usually cited as the model that Latin teachers translated.
latinIntro.cn: pronomen 与 nomen 是可靠的同源词；它们背后的希腊术语，一般认为就是拉丁语教师所模仿翻译的原型。

items.meaning: a word standing for a name
a word used in place of a noun

latinEntries.meaning: a word standing for a name

definition_zh: 发音；读作；宣判；正式宣布；断言
definition_en: to make the sound of a word or letter, or to announce something formally and officially
core_image: 嘴唇、舌头和气流一起，把纸上一串字母变成别人听得见的声音
scene: 新生点名时，老师把花名册上的名字一个个念出来，念到某个姓氏时停了一下。She paused to pronounce the unfamiliar surname slowly and clearly.
sceneCN: 这里取「发音、读出来」的意思（第 1 个义项：把词或字母读出声音）；句意为她停下来，把这个不常见的姓氏慢慢地、清楚地读了出来。花名册上那个生僻的姓就是线索。

pos.zh: 发音；读作；宣判；正式宣布；断言

derivatives.zh: 由 pronounce 加 -ment 构成，义为「公告；正式声明」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「明显的；显著的」
由同一拉丁词干的名词 pronuntiatio 经法语进入英语，义为「发音」
在 pronounce 前加表示「错误地」的前缀 mis-，义为「读错」

senses.title: To make the sound of a word or letter
senses.definition: to make the sound of a word, a name or a letter with the voice
senses.definitionCN: 用嗓音发出单词、名字或字母的读音
senses.example: Nobody in the class could pronounce her family name.
senses.exampleCN: 班上没人能读出她的姓。
senses.why: Latin nuntiare meant to announce, and pro- meant forth, so the pair first meant to bring a sound out into the open; the mouth is only the instrument that does it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nuntiare 意为「宣告」，前缀 pro- 意为「向外」，两者合起来本是「把声音送到外面」；嘴巴只是完成这件事的工具，不是词义的起点。

senses.title: To declare something officially
senses.definition: to announce a sentence, a verdict or a decision in a formal and official way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式、官方的方式宣布判决、裁定或决定
senses.example: The judge pronounced a sentence of five years.
senses.exampleCN: 法官宣判五年徒刑。
senses.why: A court does not merely think its decision, it says it aloud, and the announcing half of the Latin word survives exactly there: the sentence takes effect when it is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 法庭的判决不只是想清楚，还要念出来；拉丁词里「宣告」的那一半正好留在这种场合——判词被说出口的那一刻才生效。

senses.title: To state an opinion firmly
senses.definition: to give a firm opinion or judgement about something, often in a slightly formal tone
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给出明确而坚定的看法或评判，语气常偏正式
senses.example: The critic pronounced the film a masterpiece.
senses.exampleCN: 那位影评人断言这部电影是杰作。
senses.why: Anyone who announces a verdict is borrowing a judge's authority, so the word widened from courtrooms to critics and experts who speak as if their view were a ruling.
senses.whyCN: 宣告裁定的人都在借用法官的权威，于是这个词从法庭扩展到评论家和专家身上——他们说话时，仿佛自己的看法就是一条裁定。

senses.title: To be sounded in a particular way
senses.definition: to be sounded in the way described, said of a written word, a name or a letter
senses.definitionCN: 读音如所说的那样，用于说明写出来的单词、名字或字母怎么念
senses.example: The town's name is pronounced with the stress on the first syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇的名字重音落在第一个音节上。
senses.why: English spelling and sound often part company, so the same verb is used passively to record how a written form is actually said, with no declaring involved at all.
senses.whyCN: 英语的拼写和读音常常对不上，于是同一个动词也用被动形式来记录「写出来的形式实际怎么念」，此时完全与「宣告」无关。

intro.en: Pronounce joins a Latin prefix meaning forth to a Latin verb meaning to announce, so the word has always carried both a mouth and a public voice.
intro.cn: pronounce 把表示「向外」的拉丁语前缀接在表示「宣告」的拉丁语动词上，所以这个词从源头起就同时带着「嘴」和「公开的声音」。

items.en: Nuntiare meant to announce, to report or to bring news, and the related noun nuntius meant messenger.
items.cn: nuntiare 意为宣告、报告、带来消息，相关名词 nuntius 指信使。

items.en: Adding pro-, forth, produced pronuntiare, to speak out, to utter, and already to declare in public.
items.cn: 加上表示「向外」的 pro-，得到 pronuntiare，意为说出、发声，并且已经带有「当众宣告」的意味。

items.en: The action noun pronuntiatio named a speaking out and a declaration, and it is the ancestor of the English noun.
items.cn: 动作名词 pronuntiatio 指「说出」与「宣告」，它是英语名词 pronunciation 的祖先。

items.en: Old French softened the consonant cluster and gave the verb as prononcier, with the o of the Latin noun but no t before the ending.
items.cn: 古法语把辅音簇软化，动词写作 prononcier，保有拉丁名词里的 o，但词尾前没有 t。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the verb as pronounce and used it for sounding words and for formal declarations; the noun came separately from the Latin noun, which is why pronunciation has no o.
items.cn: 中古英语借入动词作 pronounce，既用于读词，也用于正式宣告；名词则另从拉丁名词借入，所以 pronunciation 里没有 o。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin verb for announcing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for producing words with the voice.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「宣告」动词上的形式；近义组收用嗓音说出词语的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the way a word is spoken, with no o after the n.
entries.definitionCN: 表示词的读法的名词，n 后面没有 o。

entries.definition: A formal public statement or declaration.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的公开声明或宣告。

entries.definition: To say a word in a wrong way.
entries.definitionCN: 把单词读错。

entries.definition: To make something known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 公开宣布某事。

entries.definition: To say words clearly and distinctly.
entries.definitionCN: 清晰地咬字发音。

entries.definition: To say something aloud.
entries.definitionCN: 说出；发出（声音）。

entries.definition: To form sounds clearly enough to be understood.
entries.definitionCN: 把音发清楚，使人听得懂。

entries.definition: To state something officially or firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或坚定地声明。

entries.definition: To produce words with the voice.
entries.definitionCN: 用嗓音说出词语。

normalIntro.en: The word holds a mouth and a public voice at once, and its family keeps splitting along those two lines: sounding words, and declaring things.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时握着「嘴」和「公开的声音」，同族词也沿这两条线分开：读词，以及宣告。

normal.en: Latin nuntiare also gives announce, so pronounce and announce are cousins: both bring something out where others can hear it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare 也带来 announce，所以 pronounce 与 announce 是表亲：两者都把东西送到别人听得见的地方。

normal.en: The prefix pro- means forth, so to pronounce is literally to carry a sound out of the mouth.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示「向外」，所以 pronounce 字面上就是「把声音从嘴里送出去」。

normal.en: The noun pronunciation comes from Latin pronuntiatio, not from the English verb, which is why the o of pronounce is missing there.
normal.cn: 名词 pronunciation 来自拉丁语 pronuntiatio，而不是来自英语动词，所以那里少了 pronounce 的 o。

normal.en: The adjective pronounced means noticeable, because something pronounced has been said out clearly enough to be heard.
normal.cn: 形容词 pronounced 意为「明显的」，因为被清楚说出来的东西自然引人注意。

normal.en: A judge pronounces sentence: the legal use draws on the announcing half of the word, not on the mouth.
normal.cn: 法官宣判用 pronounce sentence，这个法律用法取的是词里「宣告」的那一半，与嘴无关。

abstract.en: A word only becomes fully real when someone pronounces it; print is little more than a set of instructions for the mouth.
abstract.cn: 一个词只有被人念出来才完全成立；纸上的拼写不过是给嘴巴的一套说明。

abstract.en: Saying a verdict and saying a word share one verb because both make something official simply by speaking it.
abstract.cn: 宣读判决和读出一个词共用一个动词，因为两者都只靠「说出来」就让某事生效。

abstract.en: The distance between how a word is written and how it is pronounced is where the history of the language shows through.
abstract.cn: 一个词「怎么写」和「怎么念」之间的距离，正是这门语言的历史露出来的地方。

examples.en: Nobody in the class could pronounce her family name.
examples.cn: 班上没人能读出她的姓。

examples.en: The judge pronounced a sentence of five years.
examples.cn: 法官宣判五年徒刑。

examples.en: The town's name is pronounced with the stress on the first syllable.
examples.cn: 这个镇的名字重音落在第一个音节上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若闹恩斯」——像「扑上去念」，凑到字母跟前使劲念，就是发音。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向外）+ nuntiare（宣告）构成 pronuntiare，本义「说出、当众宣告」；动词经古法语 prononcier 进入英语作 pronounce，名词则另从拉丁语 pronuntiatio 借入。

sensesIntro.en: The core is sending a sound outward; from it grow the mouth's work of saying words, the courtroom's spoken verdict, the expert's spoken judgement, and the passive record of how a written form sounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把声音送出去」；由它长出嘴读词的动作、法庭上念出的判词、专家说出的定论，以及被动记录「写出来的形式怎么念」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lips, tongue and breath turning a line of printed letters into sound that other people can hear.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴唇、舌头和气流一起，把纸上一行字母变成别人听得见的声音。

branches.en: a teacher pointing at one letter on the board
branches.cn: 老师指着黑板上的一个字母

branches.en: a name written one way and said another
branches.cn: 写法一种、读法另一种的名字

branches.en: a courtroom where the sentence is read aloud
branches.cn: 宣读判词的法庭

branches.en: a critic closing a programme with a verdict
branches.cn: 影评人用一句定论结束节目

branches.en: words spoken as if they were final
branches.cn: 说得像终审一样的话

intro.en: A Latin prefix of outward movement and a Latin verb of announcing hold the word together, and French reshaped the verb before English took it.
intro.cn: 表示向外运动的拉丁语前缀和表示宣告的拉丁语动词共同支撑这个词，法语先在中间改造了动词形式，英语随后借入。

latinIntro.en: Latin nuntiare, to announce, and its compound pronuntiare, to speak out, are the direct sources of the English verb and of its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare（宣告）及其复合形式 pronuntiare（说出）是英语动词与名词的直接来源。

items.meaning: to sound a word, to declare

definition_zh: 发音；读音；口音；语音
definition_en: the way in which a word or a language is spoken, or a person's way of speaking
core_image: 一个词从纸上站起来，被嘴巴念成一段有重音、有长短的声音
scene: 语言课上，老师让学生把同一个单词读三遍，注意词尾那一点细微的差别。Her pronunciation of the final consonant still sounded slightly French.
sceneCN: 这里取「读音、发音方式」的意思（第 1 个义项：一个词被说出来的声音形式）；句意为她对词尾辅音的读法仍带着一点法语味道。老师反复提醒的那个词尾就是线索。

pos.zh: 发音；读音；口音；语音

derivatives.zh: 来自同一拉丁词干的动词，义为「发音；宣判」
在 pronunciation 前加表示「错误地」的前缀 mis-，义为「读错；错误发音」
由 pronounce 加 -able 与否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「念不出来的」

senses.title: The way a word or language is spoken
senses.definition: the way in which a particular word or language is spoken, including its sounds, stress and rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 某个词或某门语言被说出来的方式，包括音素、重音与节奏
senses.example: The dictionary gives two pronunciations for that word.
senses.exampleCN: 词典给这个词标了两种读音。
senses.why: The Latin noun pronuntiatio named the act of speaking out, and English borrowed that noun rather than the verb, so the word begins from the spoken form and not from the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 pronuntiatio 本指「说出来的动作」，英语借的是这个名词而不是动词，所以这个词的起点是「说出来的声音形式」，不是纸上的拼写。

senses.title: A person's way of speaking
senses.definition: the way a particular person speaks, especially as a sign of where they grew up or learned the language
senses.definitionCN: 某个人说话的方式，尤指能看出其成长地或学语言经历的特征
senses.example: His pronunciation betrayed that he had grown up abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他的口音暴露出他是在国外长大的。
senses.why: If the word names the sound of a whole language, it can also name the sound of one speaker, and in that shift it quietly takes over the work of the word accent.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指整门语言的声音，也就能指某一个说话人的声音；在这一转之中，它悄悄接手了 accent 的工作。

senses.title: Speech sounds as a subject to teach
senses.definition: the part of language teaching that deals with sounds, stress and intonation
senses.definitionCN: 语言教学中处理音素、重音与语调的那一部分内容
senses.example: She teaches pronunciation to adult learners.
senses.exampleCN: 她给成年学员上语音课。
senses.why: Once the sounds of a language can be described, marked and corrected, they become something that can be taught, which is why the word also names a subject on a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 一门语言的声音一旦能被描述、标注、纠正，就成了可以教的东西，所以这个词也指课表上的一门内容。

intro.en: Pronunciation comes straight from a Latin action noun for speaking out, and that is the reason its spelling differs from the verb it seems to belong to.
intro.cn: pronunciation 直接来自一个表示「说出」的拉丁动作名词，这正是它的拼写与看似对应的动词不一致的原因。

items.en: Nuntiare meant to announce or report, and it supplied the announcing core of the whole family.
items.cn: nuntiare 意为宣告、报告，为整族词提供了「宣告」这个核心。

items.en: With the prefix pro-, forth, the verb pronuntiare meant to speak out, to utter sounds and to declare.
items.cn: 加上表示「向外」的前缀 pro-，动词 pronuntiare 意为说出、发声、宣告。

items.en: The noun pronuntiatio named the act and manner of speaking out, and its stem pronuntiat- is what English kept.
items.cn: 名词 pronuntiatio 指说出的动作与方式，英语保留的正是它的词干 pronuntiat-。

items.en: Old French passed the noun on as prononciation, turning the Latin t before i into a soft c sound.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 prononciation，拉丁语里 i 前的 t 变成了软音 c。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as pronunciation with n-u-n, following the Latin stem; the o of pronounce never entered, because this word came from the noun, not the verb.
items.cn: 英语按拉丁词干把拼写固定为带 n-u-n 的 pronunciation；pronounce 里的 o 从未进入，因为这个词来自名词而非动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin noun of speaking out; the near-meaning group gathers words about accent, clarity and the sound of speech.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「说出」名词上的形式；近义组收关于口音、清晰度与语音的词语。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to sound a word or to declare something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示读出一个词或宣布某事的动词。

entries.definition: A wrong way of saying a word.
entries.definitionCN: 读错的发音。

entries.definition: A formal public statement.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的公开声明。

entries.definition: An announcement, especially a solemn one.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告，尤指庄重的宣告。

entries.definition: The way people from a place or group speak.
entries.definitionCN: 某地或某群体说话的腔调。

entries.definition: The clear production of speech sounds.
entries.definitionCN: 语音的清晰发出。

entries.definition: The clarity with which words are spoken or sung.
entries.definitionCN: 说话或演唱时咬字的清晰程度。

entries.definition: The rise and fall of the voice in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 说话时嗓音的升降。

normalIntro.en: The word is a mouth shaping a word into sound, and its memories sit on the Latin noun, on stress, and on the missing letter.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一张嘴把一个词念成声音，记忆点落在拉丁名词、重音，以及那个消失的字母上。

normal.en: The verb has an o after the n and the noun does not, because the noun came from Latin pronuntiatio while the verb came through French prononcier.
normal.cn: 动词在 n 后面有 o，名词没有，因为名词来自拉丁语 pronuntiatio，动词则经法语 prononcier 传来。

normal.en: The -tion ending marks a noun of action, exactly as in declaration and explanation.
normal.cn: -tion 结尾标明这是一个动作名词，就像 declaration 与 explanation 一样。

normal.en: Stress falls late, on the syllable that carries -ation, so the first syllables stay light and quick.
normal.cn: 重音落在后面带 -ation 的音节上，前面几个音节因此又轻又快。

normal.en: Mispronunciation adds mis-, wrongly, and keeps the full Latin stem, so the n-u-n stays visible.
normal.cn: mispronunciation 加上表示「错误地」的 mis-，并保留完整的拉丁词干，所以 n-u-n 清楚可见。

normal.en: Annunciation and announce share the announcing root, so this family is not only about mouths.
normal.cn: annunciation 与 announce 共享「宣告」词根，可见这一族词并不只关乎嘴。

abstract.en: Pronunciation is the part of a word that a dictionary can only approximate; the mouth always finishes the job.
abstract.cn: 发音是词典只能大致描摹的那一部分，最后的成品总要由嘴巴完成。

abstract.en: A word can be spelled one way and spoken another, and the gap between the noun and the verb is a small monument to that fact.
abstract.cn: 词可以这样写、那样念，名词与动词之间的那点差别，正是这件事留下的一个小纪念碑。

abstract.en: To judge someone by their pronunciation is to hear history, geography and family gathered into a single vowel.
abstract.cn: 凭发音判断一个人，等于从一个元音里听出历史、地理与家庭。

examples.en: The dictionary gives two pronunciations for that word.
examples.cn: 词典给这个词标了两种读音。

examples.en: His pronunciation betrayed that he had grown up abroad.
examples.cn: 他的口音暴露出他是在国外长大的。

examples.en: She teaches pronunciation to adult learners.
examples.cn: 她给成年学员上语音课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若难西」——念着就觉得有点难，越难越要练，正是发音。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向外）+ nuntiare（宣告）构成 pronuntiare，其动作名词 pronuntiatio（说出、宣告）经古法语 prononciation 进入英语；词干保留 n-u-n，所以拼写里没有 pronounce 的 o。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the spoken shape of a word; the senses divide into the sound of a word, the sound of a speaker, and the sound of a language as something to be taught.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一个词被说出来的声音形状」；义项分成一个词的读音、一个说话人的口音，以及作为教学对象的一门语言的语音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a printed word lifted off the page and shaped by the mouth into a stretch of sound with its own beat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个印在纸上的词脱离纸面，被嘴巴塑造成一段有自己节拍的声音。

branches.en: two pronunciations printed side by side in a dictionary
branches.cn: 词典里并排印出的两种读音

branches.en: a familiar word said in an unfamiliar voice
branches.cn: 熟悉词被陌生嗓音读出

branches.en: a listener guessing where a stranger grew up
branches.cn: 听者猜陌生人是在哪里长大的

branches.en: a classroom drilling one difficult consonant
branches.cn: 课堂上反复练一个难辅音

branches.en: a recording played again to catch a single sound
branches.cn: 为听清一个音再放一遍录音

intro.en: A Latin verb of announcing and the action noun built from it hold the word together; French softened the consonants and English kept the Latin stem in the spelling.
intro.cn: 表示宣告的拉丁语动词及其动作名词共同支撑这个词；法语软化了辅音，英语则在拼写上保留了拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin nuntiare, to announce, its compound pronuntiare, and the action noun pronuntiatio are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare（宣告）、其复合形式 pronuntiare 以及动作名词 pronuntiatio 是英语这个词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 证据；证明；校样；检验；防…的；能抵挡…的
definition_en: facts or evidence showing that something is true, a trial copy of printed work, or, as an adjective, able to resist something
core_image: 一样东西被反复检验过，最后摆到桌上当作凭据
scene: 实验室的桌上摊着一叠材料，研究员把每一次测量都抄进本子，好让结论站得住脚。The team needed proof that the new filter actually removed the salt.
sceneCN: 这里取「证据」的意思（第 1 个义项：能证明某事为真的材料）；句意为团队需要证据，证明新滤芯确实去掉了盐分。桌上那叠记录就是他们正在攒的东西。

pos.zh: 证据；证明；校样；检验
防…的；能抵挡…的；耐…的

derivatives.zh: 与 proof 同出拉丁词干 probare，义为「证明；证实」
由 proof 与 read 复合而成，义为「校对」
由 water 与 proof 复合而成，义为「防水的」
由拉丁词干 prob- 加 -able 构成，义为「很可能的」

senses.title: Evidence that something is true
senses.definition: facts, information or objects that show that something is true or really exists
senses.definitionCN: 能表明某事为真或确实存在的事实、信息或物件
senses.example: The police found no proof that he had been there.
senses.exampleCN: 警方没有找到他当时在场的证据。
senses.why: Latin probare meant to test and to judge as good, so a proof is literally what comes out of a test: the word names the result before it names the argument.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验并判断好坏，所以 proof 字面上就是检验之后出来的东西：它先指结果，然后才指论证。

senses.title: A logical or mathematical demonstration
senses.definition: a series of steps showing that a statement must be true, especially in mathematics or logic
senses.definitionCN: 尤其用于数学或逻辑，用一串步骤表明某个命题必然成立
senses.example: The proof took three pages and ended with a single line.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明写了三页，最后只归结为一行。
senses.why: If a proof is what a test yields, then a chain of reasoning is the strictest test available: every step checks the one before it and leaves no room for doubt.
senses.whyCN: 既然 proof 是检验的产物，那么一串推理就是最严格的检验：每一步都在核对前一步，不留怀疑的余地。

senses.title: A trial print checked for errors
senses.definition: a copy of printed or photographed work made before the final version so that mistakes can still be corrected
senses.definitionCN: 在定稿之前印出的一份副本，以便还能改正错误
senses.example: She read the proof of her article and marked two typos.
senses.exampleCN: 她读了文章的校样，标出两处排印错误。
senses.why: Printers once pulled a sheet off the press to test the type, and the sheet used for that test simply inherited the name of the test itself.
senses.whyCN: 从前印刷工要从机器上抽一张纸来验版，用来验版的那张纸就直接继承了「检验」这个名字。

senses.title: Able to resist something
senses.definition: strong enough to keep something out or to resist damage, used after a noun or with against
senses.definitionCN: 足以把某物挡在外面或不受损伤，常后置或与 against 连用
senses.example: The jacket is proof against wind and rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套防风又防雨。
senses.why: Something that has been tested and has not failed is trusted, so proof turned into an adjective for materials that have already survived the test of wind, water or fire.
senses.whyCN: 经得住检验、没有失手的东西才可信，于是 proof 转成形容词，指已经扛过风、水或火考验的材料。

senses.title: A test of quality
senses.definition: an act of testing whether something is good enough, or the standard it has to reach
senses.definitionCN: 检验某物是否够好的动作，或它必须达到的标准
senses.example: The pudding is the proof of the cook.
senses.exampleCN: 布丁好坏，一尝便知厨师本事。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word kept almost untouched: proof as the trial itself, before it came to mean the evidence that the trial produced.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层，几乎原样留着：proof 指检验这件事本身，早于它指检验得出的证据。

intro.en: Proof descends from a Latin verb meaning to test, and that testing sense still explains both the evidence and the printed sheet.
intro.cn: proof 出自一个意为「检验」的拉丁动词，正是这层「检验」的意思同时解释了「证据」与「校样」。

items.en: Probare meant to test, to examine and to judge as good, and the adjective probus described something upright and sound.
items.cn: probare 意为检验、查验、判定为好，形容词 probus 指正直、可靠的。

items.en: A noun proba grew from the verb and named a trial or a test of something's quality.
items.cn: 由动词产生名词 proba，指试验、对某物品质的检验。

items.en: Old French carried the noun on as prueve or proeve, still meaning a trial and the evidence it produced.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 prueve 或 proeve，仍指试验以及试验得出的凭据。

items.en: Middle English borrowed two forms of the same French word, and they settled into different jobs: proof for the noun, prove for the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语从同一个法语词借入两种形式，随后分工固定下来：proof 作名词，prove 作动词。

items.en: Modern English extends proof to printed proofs, mathematical proofs and, as an adjective, to materials that resist water, wind or bullets.
items.cn: 现代英语把 proof 扩展到印刷校样、数学证明，以及作形容词时指防水、防风、防弹的材料。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin stem of testing; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for what supports a claim.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「检验」词干上的词；近义组收支撑某个说法的名词。

entries.definition: To show that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某事为真；证明。

entries.definition: Likely to be true or to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能是真的或会发生的。

entries.definition: A period of testing a person's behaviour or ability.
entries.definitionCN: 考查某人表现或能力的试用期。

entries.definition: To accept something as good enough.
entries.definitionCN: 认可某事足够好。

entries.definition: Facts that support a belief or a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 支持某种看法或说法的事实。

entries.definition: A clear showing that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚地表明某事为真。

entries.definition: The act of checking that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否属实的动作。

entries.definition: A formal statement, especially in court.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指法庭上的正式陈述。

normalIntro.en: The word is a thing held up after testing, and its family keeps returning to trials, checks and the trust that follows them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一件检验之后被举起示人的东西，同族词反复回到试验、查验以及随之而来的信任。

normal.en: Latin probare means to test, so proof and prove are two branches of one testing root, not two unrelated words.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验，所以 proof 与 prove 是同一「检验」词根的两支，并非两个无关的词。

normal.en: The noun proof and the verb prove came from two forms of the same French word, which is why they differ by a single letter.
normal.cn: 名词 proof 与动词 prove 来自同一个法语词的两种形式，所以两者只差一个字母。

normal.en: Probable, probation and approve all grow from the same stem: something judged likely, a testing period, and a test passed.
normal.cn: probable、probation、approve 都长在同一词干上：被判为可能、一段考查期，以及通过了考查。

normal.en: A printing proof is the sheet pulled to test the type, so the word can name the test and the thing tested at the same time.
normal.cn: 印刷校样是为验版抽出的那张纸，所以这个词能同时指检验和被检验的东西。

normal.en: Proof as an adjective grew from proof against something: a coat proof against rain has survived the test of rain.
normal.cn: 作形容词的 proof 从 proof against 长出来：proof against rain 的外套，就是扛住了雨的考验。

abstract.en: A proof is not the truth itself but the trace a test leaves, which is why evidence and demonstration can share the word.
abstract.cn: 证据不是真理本身，而是检验留下的痕迹，所以「证据」与「论证」能共用一个词。

abstract.en: To be proof against something is a promise about the future made on the strength of a test in the past.
abstract.cn: 说某物防得住，是凭过去的检验对未来作出的承诺。

abstract.en: Every proof is addressed to someone who doubts, so the word always carries a listener inside it.
abstract.cn: 每一份证据都是说给怀疑者听的，所以这个词里始终藏着一个听众。

examples.en: The police found no proof that he had been there.
examples.cn: 警方没有找到他当时在场的证据。

examples.en: This jacket is proof against wind and rain.
examples.cn: 这件外套防风又防雨。

examples.en: She read the proof of her article and marked two typos.
examples.cn: 她读了文章的校样，标出两处排印错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑如夫」——像「扑上去验」，扑过去仔细查一遍，验出来的就是证据。

root: 拉丁语 probare（检验、验明）产生晚期拉丁语名词 proba（检验），经古法语 prueve 进入英语；名词写作 proof，动词写作 prove，本是一个词分出的两支。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a test and what it yields; the senses divide into the evidence produced, the reasoning that serves as the strictest test, the sheet tested at the press, the material that passed a test, and the test itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「检验及其结果」；义项分成检验得出的证据、最严格的一种检验即推理、印刷时被验的那张纸、通过考验的材料，以及检验这件事本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object that has been put through a test and is now held up on the table as the record of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件经过检验的东西被举到桌上，当作检验的记录。

branches.en: a folder of documents laid on a table
branches.cn: 摊在桌上的一叠文件

branches.en: a blackboard filled with numbered steps
branches.cn: 写满编号步骤的黑板

branches.en: a printed sheet with red marks in the margin
branches.cn: 页边画着红笔的校样

branches.en: a coat with rain running off it
branches.cn: 雨水顺着外套流下

branches.en: a spoon lifted from a pudding
branches.cn: 从布丁里舀起的一勺

intro.en: A Latin verb of testing and the noun it produced hold the word together; English then split the noun and the verb into two spellings.
intro.cn: 表示检验的拉丁语动词及由其产生的名词共同支撑这个词；英语随后把名词与动词分成两种拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare, to test, its adjective probus, sound, and the Late Latin noun proba, a trial, stand behind the English noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 probare（检验）、形容词 probus（可靠的）与晚期拉丁语名词 proba（检验）是英语名词与动词背后的来源。

definition_zh: 适当的；正确的；合乎礼节的；专有的；特有的；本身的
definition_en: suitable and correct for a situation, belonging to one thing alone, or, in grammar, naming a particular person or place
core_image: 一件东西落进专为它留出的那个位置，不偏不倚，正正好好
scene: 正式晚宴前，主人把刀叉一件件摆正，餐巾折好放在盘子左侧。She checked that every guest had the proper glass beside the plate.
sceneCN: 这里取「适当的、合乎场合的」意思（第 1 个义项：适合当时场合与规矩的）；句意为她逐一确认每位客人的盘边都放着该配的那只酒杯。摆正刀叉的动作就是线索。

pos.zh: 适当的；正确的；合乎礼节的；专有的；特有的；本身的

derivatives.zh: 由 proper 加 -ly 构成，义为「适当地；正确地」
由拉丁 proprietas 经法语进入英语，义为「财产；性质」
与 proper 同出拉丁 proprietas，义为「得体；礼节」
在拉丁词干 propri- 前加 ad-，义为「合适的」

senses.title: Suitable and correct for the situation
senses.definition: right or suitable for a particular situation, purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 对某种场合、用途或某人来说正确或合适的
senses.example: Use the proper tool for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 干这活要用合适的工具。
senses.why: Latin proprius meant one's own, and what belongs to a thing is exactly what fits it, so the sense slid from belonging to being the right one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，而属于某物的东西恰恰就是适合它的东西，于是词义从「属于」滑到「正是该用的那一个」。

senses.title: Belonging to one thing alone
senses.definition: belonging by nature to one particular thing, person or group and not to any other
senses.definitionCN: 天然属于某一特定事物、人或群体，而不属于其他
senses.example: This bird is proper to the island and lives nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟是该岛特有的，别处见不到。
senses.why: The root sense of own is plainest here: a quality proper to something is a quality that belongs to it and to nothing else, which is why the word so often appears with to.
senses.whyCN: 「自己的」这层本义在这里最清楚：proper to 某物的性质，就是只属于它、不属于别处的性质，所以这个词常与 to 连用。

senses.title: Strictly so called
senses.definition: used after a noun to mean the central part of a place or thing, as opposed to the area around it
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后，指某地或某物的中心部分，以区别于其外围
senses.example: The market lies outside the old town proper.
senses.exampleCN: 市场位于老城区本身之外。
senses.why: If something is its own, the word can mark the thing itself as against its outskirts, and that is exactly how the after-noun use arose.
senses.whyCN: 既然某物是「它自己的」，这个词就能标出「事物本身」以区别于外围；后置用法正是这样长出来的。

senses.title: Naming one particular individual
senses.definition: in grammar, naming a particular person, place or thing rather than a whole class of them
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指称某个特定的人、地或物，而不是一整类
senses.example: Paris is a proper noun and city is a common noun.
senses.exampleCN: Paris 是专有名词，city 是普通名词。
senses.why: A proper noun belongs to a single bearer instead of a whole class, so the grammatical term preserves the old idea of exclusive ownership.
senses.whyCN: 专有名词只属于一个承担者而不属于一整类，所以这个语法术语保留的仍是「排他地拥有」这层旧义。

senses.title: Socially correct and respectable
senses.definition: behaving in the way polite society considers correct and respectable
senses.definitionCN: 按照讲究礼数的社会所认可、体面的方式行事
senses.example: It is not proper to ask about someone's salary.
senses.exampleCN: 打听别人的薪水不合规矩。
senses.why: A community decides what belongs to a well-run occasion, so propriety became a matter of manners and the adjective took on the sense of socially correct.
senses.whyCN: 一个共同体认定什么才属于「办得体面的场合」，于是 proper 也成了举止问题，形容词便带上「合乎社交规矩」的意思。

intro.en: Proper goes back to a Latin adjective meaning one's own, and every later sense is a variation on belonging.
intro.cn: proper 上溯到一个意为「自己的」的拉丁形容词，后来所有义项都是「归属」这一点的变奏。

items.en: Proprius meant one's own, personal, not shared with others; a common but uncertain explanation derives it from pro privo, for a private person.
items.cn: proprius 意为自己的、个人的、不与他人共有的；一般认为它与 pro privo（为了私人）有关，但这一解释并不确定。

items.en: The noun proprietas named ownership and also the quality that belongs to a thing and makes it what it is.
items.cn: 名词 proprietas 指所有权，也指属于某物、使该物成为其自身的性质。

items.en: Old French propre kept the senses of one's own, suitable and also clean or neat.
items.cn: 古法语 propre 保留了「自己的」「合适的」，以及「干净整洁的」这几层意思。

items.en: Middle English proper first meant belonging to someone or something, and older texts also use it for fine or excellent.
items.cn: 中古英语的 proper 最初指「属于某人或某物的」，较早的文本里还用它表示「出色的、优良的」。

items.en: Modern English settles on suitable, exclusive and strict, and keeps the old ownership in property, propriety, appropriate and the grammatical proper noun.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义定为「合适的、专属的、严格意义上的」，并把「归属」的旧义留在 property、propriety、appropriate 以及语法术语 proper noun 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for one's own; the near-meaning group gathers words about fitting and good manners.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「自己的」形容词上的词；近义组收关于「合适」与「礼节」的词。

entries.definition: Something owned, or a quality belonging to a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有的东西，或某物具有的性质。

entries.definition: Correctness of behaviour, good manners.
entries.definitionCN: 举止得体；礼节。

entries.definition: Suitable for a particular purpose or occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 适合某用途或场合的。

entries.definition: The owner of a business or a property.
entries.definitionCN: 企业或产业的所有者。

entries.definition: Right for a purpose or a person.
entries.definitionCN: 适合某用途或某人的。

entries.definition: Appropriate to the occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 与场合相称的。

entries.definition: Polite and correct in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 举止有礼而得体的。

entries.definition: Considered decent and proper by others.
entries.definitionCN: 被他人视为正派得体的。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from ownership and ends in fitness, and the whole family still turns on the question of what belongs where.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「归属」出发，走到「合宜」，整族词始终围绕「什么该在什么位置」这一问题。

normal.en: Latin proprius means one's own, so proper is about ownership before it is ever about manners.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，所以 proper 先说归属，之后才说礼节。

normal.en: Property and propriety share the same stem: what one owns, and what it is fitting to own or to do.
normal.cn: property 与 propriety 同一词干：一个是拥有的东西，一个是拥有或行事是否得体。

normal.en: The grammatical proper noun keeps the old sense, since such a name is owned by one person or one place.
normal.cn: 语法术语 proper noun 保留了旧义，因为这类名字只被一个人或一个地方拥有。

normal.en: After a noun, as in the city proper, the word marks the thing itself rather than the area around it.
normal.cn: 放在名词后，如 the city proper，这个词标出的是事物本身，而不是它周边的地带。

normal.en: Appropriate adds ad-, to, to the same stem: to make something one's own, and therefore to make it fit.
normal.cn: appropriate 在同一词干前加 ad-（向），意为「使成为自己的」，因此也就是「使之合宜」。

abstract.en: What is proper to a thing is what cannot be taken from it without changing what it is.
abstract.cn: 某物所专属的东西，一旦被拿走，它就不再是原来的它。

abstract.en: Manners and grammar seem far apart, yet both use proper to decide what belongs where.
abstract.cn: 礼节与语法看似相隔很远，却都用 proper 来判定什么该在什么位置。

abstract.en: A word for ownership became a word for correctness because fitting in has always been a matter of belonging.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「拥有」的词变成了表示「正确」的词，因为「合宜」从来就是「归属」的另一面。

examples.en: Use the proper tool for the job.
examples.cn: 干这活要用合适的工具。

examples.en: Paris is a proper noun and city is a common noun.
examples.cn: Paris 是专有名词，city 是普通名词。

examples.en: The market lies outside the old town proper.
examples.cn: 市场位于老城区本身之外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若破」——听着像「铺得正」，铺得正正好好，就是适当。

root: 拉丁语 proprius（自己的、专属的），深层来源一般认为与「私人、个别」有关，但具体构成存疑；经古法语 propre 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is belonging, and the senses fan out from it: what fits because it belongs, what belongs to one thing only, the thing itself, a name owned by one bearer, and the manners a community expects.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「归属」，义项由它散开：因为属于所以合宜、只属于一物的特性、事物本身、只被一个对象拥有的名字，以及共同体期待的礼节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object dropping neatly into the one slot cut for it, with no gap on any side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西落进专为它挖出的那个凹槽，四边不留缝隙。

branches.en: a tool that fits the hand exactly
branches.cn: 正好合手的一把工具

branches.en: a bird found on one island only
branches.cn: 只在一座岛上出现的鸟

branches.en: a map where the old town sits inside its ring road
branches.cn: 旧城被环路围住的城区图

branches.en: a capital letter at the start of a name
branches.cn: 名字开头的那个大写字母

branches.en: a guest choosing the right fork
branches.cn: 客人挑对那把叉子

intro.en: A Latin adjective of ownership and the noun built from it hold the word together, and English suffixes turn the same stem into adverbs, nouns and related adjectives.
intro.cn: 表示归属的拉丁语形容词及由其构成的名词共同支撑这个词，英语后缀又把同一词干变成副词、名词和相关形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin proprius, one's own, and the noun proprietas, ownership or peculiar quality, are the direct sources of the English word and of its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 proprius（自己的）与名词 proprietas（所有权、特性）是英语这个词及其同族词的直接来源。

items.meaning: ownership, a quality of one's own

definition_zh: 正确地；恰当地；得体地；彻底地
definition_en: in the correct or suitable way; in a socially acceptable manner; (British, informal) completely or thoroughly
core_image: 工匠把一块木板量准、放平，直到它与墙面严丝合缝
scene: 木工把尺子贴紧墙边，反复对照图纸，确认每一块板都装在该在的位置。The carpenter checked the shelf twice to make sure it was properly fixed to the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 properly 是「正确地、恰当地」（第 1 个义项：以正确合适的方式）；句意为木匠检查了两次，确认搁板被牢牢固定在墙上。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、图纸、木搁板。

pos.zh: 正确地；恰当地；得体地；彻底地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到形容词，义为「恰当的；正确的；本身的」
与 proper 同出拉丁 proprius（自己的），义为「得体的举止；合宜」
同出拉丁 proprius（属于自己的东西），义为「财产；房产；属性」
proper 前加否定前缀 im-，义为「不恰当的；不合规矩的」

senses.title: In the correct or suitable way
senses.definition: in the way that is correct, suitable, or expected for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 以正确、合适或符合某一用途所需的方式
senses.example: The machine will not work unless it is properly connected.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器如果没有正确接通，就无法运转。
senses.why: Properly is simply proper plus -ly, so it carries the old Latin sense of something sitting in its own place and fitting there exactly.
senses.whyCN: properly 就是 proper 加 -ly，因此继承了拉丁语「待在自己位置、恰好贴合」的意思：装在该装的地方，才算正确地做。

senses.title: In a socially acceptable manner
senses.definition: in a way that follows good manners or accepted social standards
senses.definitionCN: 遵循良好礼节或公认社会标准的方式
senses.example: He was properly introduced to the guests before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚宴前，他被正式介绍给各位客人。
senses.why: If a thing belongs in its proper place, a person can also belong in the proper occasion, so the word slides from a fitted joint to fitted behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 东西有它该在的位置，人也有他该在场的场合，于是词义便从「装得对」滑向「举止合宜」。

senses.title: Completely; thoroughly (British, informal)
senses.titleCN: 彻底地；完全地（英式口语）
senses.definition: used in British informal speech to mean completely or very much
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中表示「完全地、非常」
senses.example: I was properly soaked by the time I got home.
senses.exampleCN: 等我到家时，已经浑身湿透了。
senses.why: When a job is done properly, nothing is left half-finished, so speakers began using the word for utterly or entirely, especially in British speech.
senses.whyCN: 一件事做得 properly，就意味着没有一处半途而废；英式口语便借这层「做得彻底」引申出「完全地」。

senses.title: With good reason; justifiably
senses.definition: in a way that is fair, reasonable, or deserved
senses.definitionCN: 以公平、合理或应得的方式
senses.example: She was properly proud of the garden she had raised from seed.
senses.exampleCN: 那座花园是她从种子一手养大的，她理应为之自豪。
senses.why: Something proper is fitting, and what is fitting can also be deserved, which lets the word mark fair pride or fair blame rather than mere correctness.
senses.whyCN: proper 指「合宜」，而合宜的东西也就是应得的；于是这个词能标示理所应当的自豪或责备，而不只是「正确」。

intro.en: Properly is the adverb of proper, a word that reached English from Latin proprius by way of French, with -ly added to mark the manner of doing something.
intro.cn: properly 是 proper 的副词形式；proper 经法语来自拉丁语 proprius，加上 -ly 表示做事的方式。

items.en: Proprius meant one's own, special, or belonging to a particular thing rather than to others.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、专属的」，指某物属于特定对象，而不属于别的对象。

items.en: The noun proprietas named the quality of belonging to someone, and it later split into English propriety and property.
items.cn: 名词 proprietas 表示「归属某人的性质」，后来在英语中分化出 propriety 与 property。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as propre, meaning own, suitable, or clean, and passed it into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语保留形容词 propre，意为「自己的、合适的、干净的」，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English proper meant belonging to a person or thing and also fitting or correct, the sense that survives in proper behaviour.
items.cn: 中古英语 proper 既指「属于某人或某物的」，也指「合适的、正确的」，后一义保留在 proper behaviour 中。

items.en: English added the adverb ending -ly to proper, giving properly, which marks the manner of doing something in the right way.
items.cn: 英语在 proper 后加副词后缀 -ly 得到 properly，用来标示「以正确方式做某事」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin stem proprius; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for doing something the right way.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁词干 proprius 上的词；近义组收表示「以正确方式做事」的副词。

entries.definition: Correct, suitable, or belonging to a particular thing.
entries.definitionCN: 正确的、合适的，或属于某一特定事物的。

entries.definition: Not correct, or not acceptable in polite company.
entries.definitionCN: 不正确的，或在礼貌场合不被接受的。

entries.definition: Behaviour that follows accepted social standards.
entries.definitionCN: 符合公认社会标准的举止；得体。

entries.definition: Something owned by a person, or a quality of a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 某人拥有的财物，或某物的属性。

entries.definition: In a way that is accurate and free from error.
entries.definitionCN: 准确、没有错误地。

entries.definition: In a way that suits the situation or purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 以适合情境或目的的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that is right for the occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 适合该场合地。

entries.definition: For a good reason, or in a fair way.
entries.definitionCN: 有充分理由地，或公平地。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from the Latin adjective proprius, its French descendant propre, and the ordinary English adverb ending -ly.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由拉丁形容词 proprius、它的法语后裔 propre，以及最常见的英语副词后缀 -ly 组成。

normal.en: Properly is proper plus -ly, and -ly is the ordinary English ending for the manner of an action.
normal.cn: properly 就是 proper 加 -ly，而 -ly 是英语里最常见的「做事方式」后缀。

normal.en: Something proper sits in its own place, so doing a job properly means putting every part where it belongs.
normal.cn: proper 的东西待在属于自己的位置，所以把事情做得 properly，就是把每个部分放到该放的地方。

normal.en: Improper is proper with the negative prefix im-, so improper behaviour is the exact opposite of proper behaviour.
normal.cn: improper 是 proper 前加否定前缀 im-，所以不得体的行为正是得体行为的反面。

normal.en: Property and propriety share one stem: one is what belongs to you, the other is what belongs to good manners.
normal.cn: property 与 propriety 同根：前者是归属于你的东西，后者是归属于良好礼节的东西。

normal.en: The phrase properly speaking marks the strict or exact use of a word, which is the correct sense of the adverb.
normal.cn: 短语 properly speaking 标示一个词的严格、准确用法，这正是这个副词「正确」的一面。

abstract.en: A joint that clicks into place is the whole idea of properly: no force left over, no gap left open.
abstract.cn: 一个卡进槽里的榫头就是 properly 的全部意象：用不上多余的力，也留不下一道缝。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a fitted shelf to a fitting remark, because both are judged by one question: does it belong here?
abstract.cn: 这个词可以从装好的搁板滑到一句合适的话，因为两者面对同一个判断：它属于这里吗？

abstract.en: When British speakers say properly soaked, they mean soaked through, which shows how correctness can slide into completeness.
abstract.cn: 英国人说 properly soaked 时意思是湿透，可见「正确」可以滑向「彻底」。

examples.en: The shelter must be properly anchored before the storm arrives.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临前，这个庇护所必须被妥善固定。

examples.en: She was properly dressed for the interview.
examples.cn: 她为面试穿得很得体。

examples.en: He was properly ashamed of what he had said.
examples.cn: 他对自己说过的话理当感到羞愧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普若婆利」——把每样东西摆回它该在的地方，事情才算做得对。

root: 拉丁语 proprius（自己的、专属的）→ 古法语 propre → 英语 proper；proper 加副词后缀 -ly 得 properly，义为「以正确、合宜的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is fitting into the right place; from there the word spreads to social manners, to complete thoroughness, and to what is deserved.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装进正确的位置」；义项由此扩展到社交礼节、彻底的完成，以及理所应得。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board measured, levelled and fixed so that it sits exactly where it should.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木板被量准、找平、固定，正好落在它该在的位置。

branches.en: a shelf fixed with a level and a tape measure
branches.cn: 用水平尺和卷尺装好的搁板

branches.en: a guest greeted in the right order at dinner
branches.cn: 晚宴上按次序向客人致意

branches.en: rain soaking a coat through to the lining
branches.cn: 雨水把外套从里到外浸透

branches.en: a gardener standing back from a bed she raised
branches.cn: 园丁退后一步，看着自己养大的花圃

branches.en: one word judging a fitted joint and a fair pride
branches.cn: 同一个词既评判装好的接缝，也评判应得的自豪

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin adjective proprius, its French descendant propre, and the English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁形容词 proprius、它的法语后裔 propre，以及英语副词后缀 -ly 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 财产；所有物；房产；不动产；性质；特性
definition_en: something owned, especially land or buildings, or a quality that belongs to a thing
core_image: 一块地界石立在草地边缘，石面刻着主人的记号，旁边摆着屋内可搬动的器物
scene: 遗产清册上，房子、田地与家具都列在同一栏，标明归谁所有。The estate inventory listed the house, the land and the furniture in one column, each item marked as property belonging to a named heir.
sceneCN: 这里指「归某人所有的财物与地产」，对应第 1 个义项：被拥有、可被继承的物；句意为清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏并注明归属。画面要点：地界石、主人的记号、并列的器物；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 财产；所有物；房产（不可数，指财物总体；表示一件件具体物品时可用复数）
性质；特性（可数，常用于科学语境，指某物固有的属性）

derivatives.zh: 所有人；业主（表示「自己的」词根加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）
恰当的；本身的（由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词经法语传入，语义由「属于自己的」转为「合乎其本性的」）

senses.title: Things that belong to someone
senses.definition: the things a person owns, taken as a whole, including goods, money and rights
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所拥有的东西的总和，包括货物、金钱与权利
senses.example: The estate inventory listed the house, the land and the furniture in one column, each item marked as property belonging to a named heir.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏，每件都注明属于某位继承人的财产。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'one's own', so the word begins as a label for whatever answers the question 'whose is it'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「自己的」，因此这个词起初就是给「这是谁的」这一问题的答案贴标签。

senses.title: Land and buildings
senses.definition: real estate, especially a house or plot that can be bought, sold or rented
senses.definitionCN: 不动产，尤指可买卖或出租的房屋或地块
senses.example: Property prices rose along the new railway.
senses.exampleCN: 新铁路沿线的房价上涨了。
senses.why: Land is the one thing that cannot be carried away, so it became the clearest test of who owns what.
senses.whyCN: 土地是唯一搬不走的东西，因此它成为「谁拥有什么」最清楚的检验。

senses.title: The right of ownership itself
senses.definition: the legal power to use, exclude others from, sell or give away a thing
senses.definitionCN: 使用某物、排除他人、出售或赠予该物的法律权力
senses.example: Property is a bundle of rights, not merely the object held.
senses.exampleCN: 所有权是一束权利，而不只是手中所持之物。
senses.why: Lawyers separate the object from the right over it, and the word covers both, which is why one can own property in property.
senses.whyCN: 法学家把物与对物的权利分开，而这个词同时覆盖两者，所以人可以对财产享有财产权。

senses.title: A quality belonging to a thing
senses.definition: a characteristic that a substance or object has, such as colour, hardness or conductivity
senses.definitionCN: 某物质或物体所具有的特征，如颜色、硬度或导电性
senses.example: The property that makes the alloy useful is its resistance to heat.
senses.exampleCN: 使这种合金有用的性质是它的耐热性。
senses.why: What belongs to a thing in the oldest sense includes not only goods but traits, because a trait is also something 'its own'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老意义上的「属于」不只包括财物，也包括特征，因为特征同样是某物「自己的」东西。

senses.title: Property in intangible things
senses.definition: ownership of ideas, marks, designs or other intangibles protected by law
senses.definitionCN: 对思想、标记、设计或其他受法律保护的无形之物的所有权
senses.example: A song can be property even though nothing physical is held.
senses.exampleCN: 一首歌可以是财产，尽管手中并未握着任何实体。
senses.why: If ownership is a legal relation rather than a physical grip, it can attach to what cannot be touched.
senses.whyCN: 如果所有权是一种法律关系而不是一把握持，它就能附着在摸不到的东西上。

senses.title: Objects used on a stage
senses.definition: the movable articles that an actor handles in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 演员在戏剧或影片中操作的可移动物件
senses.example: The props master checks every property before the curtain rises.
senses.exampleCN: 道具管理员在幕启前检查每一件道具。
senses.why: The theatre borrowed the legal word for 'things owned by the company', shortened it, and kept the sense of objects that belong to a production.
senses.whyCN: 剧院借用了「剧团所有的物件」这一法律说法，把它缩短，保留了「属于某场演出之物」的意思。

senses.title: An attribute in logic and mathematics
senses.definition: a feature that may be predicated of an object, or a rule that a mathematical structure satisfies
senses.definitionCN: 可以述说某一对象的特征，或某一数学结构所满足的规则
senses.example: The proof uses a property shared by all prime numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 该证明用到所有素数共有的一个属性。
senses.why: The quality sense, pushed to its most abstract, becomes whatever can be said to belong to a class of objects.
senses.whyCN: 「性质」义被推到最抽象处，就成为一切可以说属于某类对象的特征。

senses.title: An estate or domain in older use
senses.definition: a landed estate with its house and lands, especially in historical and literary descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 连同宅邸与土地在内的地产，尤见于历史与文学描写
senses.example: The old property passed to the younger son.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧庄园传给了小儿子。
senses.why: Before land became a commodity it was an inherited domain, and that older meaning survives in descriptions of country estates.
senses.whyCN: 在土地成为商品之前，它是承袭而来的领地，这一较早的含义仍保留在对乡间地产的描写中。

intro.en: Property comes from Latin proprietas 'ownership, quality', from proprius 'one's own'. The deeper origin of proprius is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been suggested but not settled. English took the word through Old French.
intro.cn: property 出自拉丁语 proprietas「所有权、性质」，源头为 proprius「自己的」。proprius 的更深来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但未成定论。英语经古法语吸收此词。

items.en: Proprius meant 'one's own, particular, not shared'; its own origin is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been proposed rather than proved.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、特有的、不共享的」；它本身的来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但这只是提出而非证实。

items.en: Proprietas named both ownership and the quality that belongs to a thing, so the two later English senses were present from the start.
items.cn: proprietas 同时指所有权与某物固有的性质，因此后来英语中的两个义项从一开始就已存在。

items.en: Old French proprete carried both senses into English, where the legal and material side soon became dominant.
items.cn: 古法语 proprete 把两个义项都带入英语，其中法律与财物的一面很快占据主导。

items.en: In Middle English the word could still mean a quality, but land, goods and the right over them increasingly answered to it.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个词仍可指性质，但土地、货物以及对它们的权利越来越多地用它来表达。

items.en: In modern usage the material sense dominates law and everyday speech, while the quality sense survives mainly in science and logic. The date of this separation is approximate.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，财物义主导法律与日常表达，而性质义主要保存在科学与逻辑中。这一分家的年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective for 'one's own' but has drifted into fitness, decorum and exclusivity; the second group gives near alternatives for belongings and for qualities.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个表示「自己的」拉丁形容词构成，但已漂向合适、得体与独占；第二组是「财物」与「性质」两个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: Correct or suitable, and in some phrases meaning 'itself'; the sense moved from 'belonging to a thing' to 'fitting that thing'.
entries.definitionCN: 正确的、合适的，在某些短语中意为「本身」；语义由「属于某物」转为「合乎某物」。

entries.definition: Correctness of behaviour or of usage; it comes from the same source but describes what is fitting rather than what is owned.
entries.definitionCN: 行为或用语得体；它出自同一来源，但描述合乎礼仪之事，而不是被拥有之物。

entries.definition: Owned by a particular person or firm, or sold under an exclusive name; it is the adjective built on the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由特定个人或公司所有的，或以独占名称销售的；它是建立在所有权义上的形容词。

entries.definition: The plural means several pieces of real estate or several qualities; the theatre shortening props belongs here too.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式可指数处房产或数种性质；剧院用语中的缩略形式也归在这里。

entries.definition: The fact of having something in one's control; it can exist without legal ownership, which is why the two are distinguished in law.
entries.definitionCN: 某物处于某人控制之下的事实；它可以没有法律上的所有权而存在，因此法律上把两者区分开。

entries.definition: Anything of value owned, seen from the balance sheet; it is a financial category rather than a legal relation.
entries.definitionCN: 所拥有的任何有价值之物，从资产负债表的角度看；它是一个财务类别，而不是法律关系。

entries.definition: A large area of land with a house, or the total property a person leaves at death; it is narrower than the entry word.
entries.definitionCN: 带有宅邸的大片土地，或某人去世时留下的全部财产；它比本词窄。

entries.definition: A characteristic regarded as belonging to a person or thing; it covers the quality sense of the entry word but never the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为属于某人或某物的特征；它覆盖本词的性质义，却从不覆盖所有权义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for 'one's own', real derived words and real legal phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词、真实派生词与真实法律用语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Everything starts from the question 'whose is it', which is what 'one's own' answers.
normal.cn: 一切都从「这是谁的」这个问题开始，而「自己的」正是它的答案。

normal.en: The family runs proper, propriety, proprietor, proprietary and proprietorship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括恰当的、得体、所有人、专有的与所有权。

normal.en: The same word covers the object and the right over it, so lawyers speak of property in property.
normal.cn: 同一个词既覆盖物，也覆盖对物的权利，因此法学家会说对财产享有财产权。

normal.en: Land is the clearest property because it cannot be carried away.
normal.cn: 土地是最清楚的财产，因为它搬不走。

normal.en: The theatre shortened the word to props, and the stage sense is still alive.
normal.cn: 剧院把这个词缩短为「道具」，舞台义至今仍活在使用中。

abstract.en: Picture a stone at the edge of a field with a name cut into it, and a chair, a cup and a coat laid beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象田野边缘一块刻着名字的石头，旁边摆着一把椅子、一只杯子和一件外套。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent box around an idea, marked with the same seal as the house.
abstract.cn: 想象一个透明的盒子罩住一个想法，盒上盖着与房屋相同的印章。

abstract.en: Picture a substance whose label reads not 'mine' but 'this is what I am like'.
abstract.cn: 想象一种物质的标签上写的不是「我的」，而是「我本来就是这样」。

examples.en: The firm owns property in three cities.
examples.cn: 这家公司在三座城市拥有房产。

examples.en: Hardness is a property that the alloy keeps at high temperature.
examples.cn: 硬度是这种合金在高温下仍保持的一种性质。

examples.en: The lease set out who was responsible for repairs to the property.
examples.cn: 租约列明了谁负责该房产的修缮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破坡地」——坡上那块地也是家产；再记住同一词还能指物之本性，就像地有坡、铁有硬。

root: 拉丁语 proprius「自己的、特有的」→ proprietas「所有权、性质」→ 经古法语 proprete 进入英语。proprius 的更深来源不确定，出自「为个体所有」短语的说法属假说；同根词包括 proper、propriety、proprietor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings grow from what answers 'whose is it'. The owned things come first, with land and buildings as the clearest case; then the right of ownership itself, which can attach even to untouchable things; then the quality that belongs to a thing, at home in science and logic; and finally the stage objects and the older landed estate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「这是谁的」这一答案长出。先是被拥有的东西，其中土地与房屋最清楚；其次是对物享有所有权的权利，它甚至可以附着在摸不到的东西上；再其次是某物固有的性质，在科学与逻辑中安家；最后是舞台道具与较早的地产庄园义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone with a name on it, and the things inside the line that answer to that name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块刻着名字的地界石，以及界线之内属于这个名字的一切。

branches.en: THINGS: belongings in general, and the objects a theatre company owns for a production.
branches.cn: 物：一般意义上的财物，以及剧团为某场演出所拥有的物件。

branches.en: LAND: the immovable core, houses and plots that cannot be carried off.
branches.cn: 土地：不可移动的内核，搬不走的房屋与地块。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: ownership as a legal power, extending to intangibles such as songs and marks.
branches.cn: 权利：作为法律权力的所有权，可延伸到歌曲与标记等无形之物。

branches.en: QUALITY: what belongs to a thing's nature, in the laboratory and in logic.
branches.cn: 性质：属于某物本性的东西，在实验室里也在逻辑中。

branches.en: ESTATE: the older landed domain, inherited rather than traded.
branches.cn: 庄园：较早的领地，承袭而来而非买卖所得。

intro.en: One Latin adjective for 'one's own' supplies the whole family, with noun and agent endings added; the sense splits between what is owned and what a thing is like.
intro.cn: 一个表示「自己的」的拉丁形容词提供了整个家族，随后加上名词与施事后缀；语义在「被拥有之物」与「某物像什么」之间分开。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the adjective, its abstract noun and the neuter form used as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了这个形容词、它的抽象名词，以及作名词用的中性形式。

items.example: The property passed to the eldest child.
The two properties share a fence.
items.exampleCN: 这两处房产共用一道篱笆。

items.example: That is the proper way to fold the cloth.
items.exampleCN: 那才是折这块布的正确方法。

items.example: The machine must be properly sealed.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器必须妥善密封。

items.example: The guests observed the proprieties of the house.
items.exampleCN: 客人们遵守这户人家的礼节。

items.meaning: the owner of a business or estate
items.example: The proprietor greeted us at the door.
The software is proprietary and cannot be copied.
items.exampleCN: 该软件为专有软件，不得复制。

items.example: The business is under sole proprietorship.

items.meaning: to take as one's own; suitable
items.example: The council appropriated funds for the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 议会拨出款项用于这座桥。

latinEntries.meaning: a thing of one's own; a characteristic

derivatives.zh: 所有人；业主（表示「自己的」词根加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）

definition_zh: 比例；部分；份额；均衡；相称；（数学）比例式；大小、规模
definition_en: the relation between parts, or between a part and the whole, in size, amount, or importance
core_image: 一块蛋糕被切成大小不同的几份，每一份与整块之间都有固定的比
scene: 建筑师在图纸上反复比较窗户与墙面。If the window is too large the wall looks light and unstable, so the proportion of glass to brick has to be judged by eye.
sceneCN: 这里 proportion 是「比例、相称」（第 2 个义项：各部之间在大小上的关系）；句意：窗太大墙面就显得轻浮不稳，所以玻璃与砖的比例只能靠眼睛来把握。图中可辨识物件：建筑立面图、窗户、墙面分区、比例尺、铅笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 比例；部分；份额；均衡；规模

按比例地
