senses.title: A part relative to the whole
senses.definition: a part considered in relation to the whole amount
senses.definitionCN: 相对于整体而言的一部分
senses.example: A large proportion of students commute.
senses.exampleCN: 很大比例的学生通勤。
senses.why: Latin proportio joins pro- 'according to' to portio 'share'. The word begins with shares: one part measured against the whole it belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proportio 把 pro-“按照”与 portio“份额”结合。这个词始于份额：一部分相对于它所属的整体被衡量。

senses.title: The relation between parts
senses.definition: the comparative size or amount of two or more parts
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个部分在大小或数量上的对比关系
senses.example: The proportion of sugar to flour matters.
senses.exampleCN: 糖与面粉的比例很关键。
senses.why: Two parts can be compared without a whole: this is the relational core. Cooking, chemistry, and design all depend on the ratio between ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 两部分可以脱离整体比较：这是关系性的核心。烹饪、化学与设计都依赖配料之间的比率。

senses.title: Correct balance or harmony
senses.definition: the quality of parts fitting together well
senses.definitionCN: 各部分彼此协调得当的性质
senses.example: The room has a pleasing sense of proportion.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间有种悦目的比例感。
senses.why: Aesthetics evaluates the relation: some ratios look right, others jar. Proportion becomes a judgment, not just a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 美学评估这种关系：某些比率看起来对，另一些则刺眼。proportion 于是成了判断，而不只是测量。

senses.title: An equal share (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a share allotted to each person
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：分给每个人的一份
senses.example: Each heir received a proportion of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 每位继承人分得遗产的一份。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the simple share: portio is a portion. The mathematical sense grew from comparing such shares.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是简单的份额：portio 就是一份。数学义从比较这些份额生长出来。

senses.title: An equation of ratios (mathematics)
senses.definition: a statement that two ratios are equal
senses.definitionCN: 两个比率相等的陈述
senses.example: Solve the proportion 3/4 = x/12.
senses.why: Mathematics formalizes the comparison: a proportion asserts an equality between two ratios. The word keeps its 'share' root even in algebra.
senses.whyCN: 数学把比较形式化：比例式断言两个比率的相等。即使在代数中，这个词仍保留“份额”词根。

senses.title: Direct or inverse proportion
senses.definition: a relationship in which one quantity changes at a fixed rate with another
senses.definitionCN: 一个量随另一个量按固定比率变化的关系
senses.example: Speed is in direct proportion to distance over time.
senses.exampleCN: 速度与距离除以时间成正比。
senses.why: Science uses proportion for lawful co-variation: as one rises, the other rises or falls by a fixed factor. The ratio becomes a law of nature.
senses.whyCN: 科学用 proportion 指有规律的共变：一个上升，另一个按固定倍数上升或下降。比率成了自然法则。

senses.title: Size or dimensions
senses.definition: the size or scale of something, especially its relative dimensions
senses.definitionCN: 某物的大小或尺度，尤指相对维度
senses.example: The sculpture has heroic proportions.
senses.exampleCN: 这座雕塑体量宏伟。
senses.why: Proportions in the plural name the measured dimensions of a body or building. The relation becomes the thing itself: a person of large proportions.
senses.whyCN: 复数 proportions 命名身体或建筑被量出的维度。关系变成了事物本身：a person of large proportions。

senses.title: Proportional representation
senses.definition: an electoral system in which seats are allotted in proportion to votes
senses.definitionCN: 按得票比例分配席位的选举制度
senses.example: The party favors proportional representation.
senses.exampleCN: 该党支持比例代表制。
senses.why: Politics applies the ratio to power: votes are shares, and seats should mirror them. The word becomes a principle of fairness.
senses.whyCN: 政治把比率用于权力：选票是份额，席位应映照它们。这个词成了一种公平原则。

senses.title: Analogy or relation (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a correspondence or analogy between things
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：事物之间的对应或类比关系
senses.example: The proportion between microcosm and macrocosm was a medieval theme.
senses.exampleCN: 小宇宙与大宇宙的对应是中世纪的主题。
senses.why: Old philosophy used proportion for cosmic correspondences, not just numbers. The word could mean 'analogy', which is why proportionality once carried metaphysical weight.
senses.whyCN: 旧哲学用 proportion 指宇宙对应，而非只是数字。这个词曾可指“类比”，所以 proportional 一度带有形而上学分量。

intro.en: Proportion is a share word before it is a math word. Latin proportio joins pro- 'according to' with portio 'share', so it names the relation between allotments. Mathematics later made that relation exact.
intro.cn: proportion 先是份额词，然后才是数学词。拉丁语 proportio 把 pro-“按照”与 portio“份额”结合，因此它命名分配物之间的关系。数学后来把这种关系精确化。

items.en: First recorded as 'relation, correspondence, comparative share', from Latin proportio.
items.cn: 最早记录为“关系、对应、比较中的份额”，来自拉丁语 proportio。

items.en: proportio(nem) 'comparative relation, analogy' = pro- 'according to, for' + portio 'a share, a part'.
items.cn: proportio(nem)“比较关系、类比”= pro-“按照、为了”+ portio“份额、部分”。

items.en: portio 'a share' also gives portion, apportion, and proportion. The family is about dividing something into parts.
items.cn: portio“份额”还生成 portion、apportion、proportion。这个词族关乎把某物分成部分。

items.en: Here pro- does not mean 'forward' as in proceed or project; it means 'according to, in relation to'. The same prefix has several senses.
items.cn: 此处 pro- 不表示 proceed 或 project 中的“向前”，而表示“按照、相对于”。同一前缀有多种含义。

items.en: The mathematical and aesthetic senses become precise: proportion in geometry, and proportion in art and architecture.
items.cn: 数学与美学义变得精确：几何中的比例，以及艺术与建筑中的比例。

items.en: Modern English uses proportion for shares, ratios, balance, size, and electoral systems, all tracing back to portio.
items.cn: 现代英语用 proportion 指份额、比率、均衡、规模与选举制度，全部追溯到 portio。

note.en: The first group shares the portio stem; the second is about nouns that also mean a ratio or a share.
note.cn: 第一组共享 portio 词干，第二组看同样表示“比率”或“份额”的名词。

entries.definition: a share or piece of something. It is the simple noun behind proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 一份或一块。它是 proportion 背后的简单名词。

entries.definition: changing at a fixed ratio with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 与某物按固定比率变化的。

entries.definition: to divide and distribute shares. It is ad- 'to' + portio.
entries.definitionCN: 分配份额。它是 ad-“向”+ portio。

entries.definition: the numerical relation between two quantities. It is the measured form of proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 两个数量之间的数值关系。它是 proportion 的测量形式。

entries.definition: a portion given to one person. It names the piece, not the relation between pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 分给一个人的一份。它命名那块，而非块与块的关系。

entries.definition: an even distribution of parts or forces. It matches the aesthetic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 部分或力量的均衡分布。它对应美学义。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin portio 'share', pro- 'according to', the portion/apportion family, and the phrases in proportion to and out of proportion.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 portio“份额”、pro-“按照”、portion/apportion 词族，以及 in proportion to / out of proportion 两个短语。

normal.en: Portio means 'share'. Proportion is the relation between shares: this part against that part, or part against whole.
normal.cn: portio 意为“份额”。proportion 是份额之间的关系：这份对那份，或部分对整体。

normal.en: Here pro- means 'according to', not 'forward'. Proportion is measured according to the shares.
normal.cn: 此处 pro- 意为“按照”，不是“向前”。proportion 是按份额来衡量的。

normal.en: In proportion to means a fixed ratio holds; out of proportion means the ratio has broken, often in emotion.
normal.cn: in proportion to 意为固定比率成立；out of proportion 意为比率破裂，常用于情绪。

normal.en: A sense of proportion is a sense of relative size: knowing what matters how much.
normal.cn: a sense of proportion 是对相对大小的感觉：知道什么值多少。

normal.en: Proportional representation makes seats mirror votes: the political version of the same ratio.
normal.cn: 比例代表制让席位映照选票：同一比率在政治中的版本。

abstract.en: Proportion is how meaning is made from relation: nothing is large or small except against something else.
abstract.cn: 比例是从关系生成意义的方式：没有东西是大或小，除非相对他物。

abstract.en: A sense of proportion is a moral skill as much as an aesthetic one: it is knowing what deserves how much attention.
abstract.cn: 分寸感既是审美技能也是道德技能：知道什么该得到多少注意。

abstract.en: The word moves from shares to ratios to justice: fair distribution and exact measurement share one root.
abstract.cn: 这个词从份额走到比率再走到正义：公平分配与精确测量共享一个词根。

examples.en: The proportion of women in the workforce has risen.
examples.cn: 女性在劳动力中的比例上升了。

examples.en: Try to keep the problem in proportion.
examples.cn: 尽量把问题看得合乎分寸。

examples.en: The two quantities are in direct proportion.
examples.cn: 这两个量成正比。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若剖身”——把整体扑开、剖开身子分成几份 → proportion 比例、份额

root: 拉丁语 proportio“比较关系”，由 pro-“按照”+ portio“份额”构成；portio 还生成 portion、apportion。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of proportion, all resting on a share. The share can be compared to the whole, to another share, to an ideal balance, to a mathematical law, to a body's size, or to a vote.
sensesIntro.cn: proportion 的九个义项都建立在“份额”上。这个份额可以相对整体、相对另一份、相对理想均衡、相对数学规律、相对身体大小，或相对选票。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: parts measured against one another and against the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：各部分彼此衡量，也与整体衡量。

branches.en: SHARE: one part set against the whole, or allotted to one person.
branches.cn: 份额：一部分相对整体，或分给一个人。

branches.en: RATIO: parts compared with each other, in arithmetic and in natural law.
branches.cn: 比率：部分彼此比较，在算术与自然法则中皆然。

branches.en: BALANCE: the relation judged as harmonious or fitting.
branches.cn: 均衡：这种关系被判断为和谐、得当。

branches.en: SIZE AND ANALOGY: measured dimensions, and the older idea of correspondence.
branches.cn: 大小与类比：被量出的维度，以及较早的对应观念。

branches.en: POLITICS: seats allotted in proportion to votes, making the ratio a rule of justice.
branches.cn: 政治：席位按选票比例分配，使比率成为正义规则。

intro.en: Proportion is a noun from Latin proportio. English adds -al, -ate, -ality, and the negative dis-, while portio also gives portion and apportion.
intro.cn: proportion 是来自拉丁 proportio 的名词。英语加 -al、-ate、-ality 与否定 dis-，portio 还生成 portion 与 apportion。

latinIntro.en: Latin proportio 'comparative relation' joins pro- 'according to' with portio 'share'. The portio family is about dividing into parts, which is why the word can mean both a ratio and a fair share.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proportio“比较关系”把 pro-“按照”与 portio“份额”结合。portio 词族关乎分成部分，所以这个词既能指比率，也能指公平份额。

definition_en: changing in step with something else, so that the relation between the two amounts stays the same

scene: 各地区的投入与产出大致成正比。Investment and output in each region are roughly proportional to one another.
sceneCN: 这里 proportional 是「与……相称的」（第 6 个义项：处罚与造成的损害成比例）；句意：罚款与该公司对河流造成的损害相称。图中可辨识物件：天平两端、按同一斜率升降的两根柱子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 成比例的；相称的；按比例分配的；比例代表制的

derivatives.zh: 比例；部分；使成比例
按比例地
相称的；成比例的
不成比例的；过大或过小的

senses.title: Changing together at a fixed rate
senses.definition: increasing or decreasing at a rate that keeps a constant relation with another quantity
senses.definitionCN: 以与另一数量保持恒定关系的速率增减
senses.example: Pressure is proportional to depth, so it doubles when the depth doubles.
senses.exampleCN: 压力与深度成正比，因此深度加倍时压力也加倍。
senses.why: Pro portione meant 'according to the share'. When two quantities keep their shares aligned, each change in one is matched by a fixed change in the other.
senses.whyCN: pro portione 意为“按份额”。当两个数量保持份额对齐时，一个量的每次变化都由另一个量的固定变化来配平。

senses.title: In due balance
senses.definition: having parts of a size that suits one another and the whole
senses.definitionCN: 各部分大小彼此相称、也与整体相称
senses.example: The architect chose a proportional height for the columns to keep the hall calm.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师为柱子选了相称的高度，让大厅显得沉稳。
senses.why: The same shares idea applies to parts of a design: a proportional building has no part that looks too big or too small for the rest.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“份额”观念适用于设计的各部分：比例恰当的建筑，没有哪一部分相对其余显得过大或过小。

senses.title: Mathematical proportion
senses.titleCN: 数学意义上的比例关系
senses.definition: describing quantities whose ratio is constant, or a term in that relation
senses.definitionCN: 指比值恒定的量，或处于该关系中的项
senses.example: In the table, the two columns are proportional, with each entry twice the one beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 表中两列成比例，每一条目都是旁边那一条的两倍。
senses.why: Mathematics fixed the word to the constant ratio. A proportional relation is one where doubling one side always doubles the other.
senses.whyCN: 数学把词固定到恒定比值上：成比例的关系，就是一边加倍时另一边必然加倍。

senses.title: Seats shared by vote share
senses.definition: of an electoral system: allocating seats in rough proportion to the votes each party wins
senses.definitionCN: 指按各党所得选票的比例分配议席的选举制度
senses.example: Under proportional representation, a party with a fifth of the vote gains about a fifth of the seats.
senses.exampleCN: 在比例代表制下，得票五分之一的政党约获得五分之一的席位。
senses.why: Electoral reformers borrowed the arithmetic of shares: seats should follow votes as closely as the two columns in a proportional table.
senses.whyCN: 选举改革者借用了份额的算术：席位应尽可能贴着选票走，就像比例表里的两列。

senses.title: Punishment that matches the harm
senses.definition: of a penalty or response: of a size that fits the wrong done or the risk created
senses.definitionCN: 指处罚或回应的大小与过错或造成的风险相称
senses.example: Judges aim for a sanction proportional to the seriousness of the offence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官力求制裁与罪行的严重程度相称。
senses.why: Here proportion is moral rather than numerical: the response should weigh the same as the harm on some shared scale.
senses.whyCN: 这里的比例是道德性的而非数字性的：回应应在某种共同标尺上与损害等重。

senses.title: Scaled to fit
senses.definition: enlarged or reduced so that every part keeps its original relation to the others
senses.definitionCN: 放大或缩小后各部分仍保持原有相互关系
senses.example: The model is proportional to the bridge but only one fiftieth of its length.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型与那座桥成比例，但长度只有其五十分之一。
senses.why: Anything scaled proportionally keeps every ratio intact. Only one measurement changes; all the others follow it exactly.
senses.whyCN: 任何等比缩放都保留全部比值，只改变一个尺寸，其余尺寸精确跟随。

senses.title: Shared out by shares
senses.definition: divided among people or groups according to an agreed share rather than equally
senses.definitionCN: 按约定份额而非平均地分给人或群体
senses.example: The profits were proportional to each partner's investment.
senses.exampleCN: 利润按每位合伙人的出资比例分配。
senses.why: Distribution is the oldest share sense: each claimant receives the fraction that belongs to them, no more and no less.
senses.whyCN: 分配是最古老的份额义：每个索取者得到属于自己的那一份，不多也不少。

senses.title: Sampled at the same rate
senses.definition: of a sample or statistics: drawn or weighted so that each subgroup appears in its true share
senses.definitionCN: 指抽样或加权使各子群按其真实份额出现
senses.example: The survey used a proportional sample so that rural districts were not undercounted.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查采用按比例抽样，以免农村地区被少算。
senses.why: Statistics repeats the share logic: if a group is a third of the population, a proportional sample makes it a third of the respondents.
senses.whyCN: 统计学重复份额逻辑：如果某群体占人口三分之一，按比例抽样就让它占受访者的三分之一。

intro.en: Proportional goes back to the Latin phrase pro portione, 'according to the share'. Portio meant a portion or allotted part, and the derived noun proportio named the relation between shares. Late Latin added the adjective proportionalis, which passed through French into English.
intro.cn: proportional 可回溯到拉丁短语 pro portione“按份额”。portio 意为一份或分得的部分，派生名词 proportio 命名各份之间的关系。晚期拉丁语再加形容词 proportionalis，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Portio meant 'a share, a part assigned'. It is the noun that carries the whole idea of dividing something into due parts.
items.cn: portio 意为“份额、分得的部分”。正是这个名词承载了把某物分成应得各份的整个观念。

items.en: The phrase meant 'according to the share'. Cicero and later writers used it for relations in which each part receives its due amount.
items.cn: 这个短语意为“按份额”。西塞罗及后来的作者用它指每一部分各得其应有数量的关系。

items.en: The phrase hardened into the noun proportio, 'comparative relation, analogy'. It covered both arithmetic ratios and fitting arrangement.
items.cn: 这个短语凝固成名词 proportio“比较关系、类比”，既涵盖算术比值，也涵盖恰当的排列。

items.en: Late Latin built the adjective proportionalis from proportio. French proportionnel then supplied the English form in the 16th century.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语由 proportio 造出形容词 proportionalis，法语 proportionnel 随后在 16 世纪提供了英语形式。

items.en: The growth of algebra and geometry fixed proportional to the constant-ratio sense, giving the precise phrase directly proportional.
items.cn: 代数与几何的发展把 proportional 固定到恒定比值义，产生了精确说法“成正比的”。

items.en: Proportional representation was debated from the mid-19th century, and sampling theory made proportional allocation a standard statistical tool.
items.cn: 比例代表制自 19 世纪中叶起被讨论，抽样理论则使按比例分配成为标准统计工具。

note.en: The look-alike group separates proportional from proportion, the adverb and the near-twin proportionate. The meaning group contrasts matching rates, matching sizes and matching shares.
note.cn: 形近组区分 proportional 与名词 proportion、副词及近似的 proportionate；词义组比较“比率相配”“大小相配”与“份额相配”。

entries.definition: a share or a relation between parts. It is the base noun, while proportional is the adjective built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 份额或各部分之间的关系。它是基础名词，proportional 是由它构成的形容词。

entries.definition: in a way that follows a proportion. It tells how something changes or is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 按比例地。它说明某物如何变化或如何分配。

entries.definition: of a size that fits or is fair. It often shades toward suitability, while proportional leans toward arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 大小合适或公平的。它常偏向“适宜”，而 proportional 偏向算术。

entries.definition: a statement or an offer. It looks close but comes from pro- plus ponere 'to put', not from portio 'share'.
entries.definitionCN: 陈述或提议。它看起来相近，却来自 pro- 加 ponere“放置”，而非 portio“份额”。

entries.definition: corresponding in size or degree, often with a note of fairness. It is the usual word for a fitting response.
entries.definitionCN: 在大小或程度上相对应的，常含公平意味。它是“恰当回应”的常用词。

entries.definition: equal in measure to something, as of pay and responsibility. It stresses matching a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 在尺度上与某物相当，如薪酬与责任。它强调与某一标准相配。

entries.definition: considered in relation to something else. It says a comparison exists, not that the ratio is fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于某物来考虑的。它只说明存在比较，不说明比值固定。

entries.definition: matching or analogous in position or function. It pairs items without implying a fixed ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 在位置或功能上对应或类似的。它配对项目，但不暗示固定比值。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to the Latin share, then let the same idea run through ratios, design, elections, penalties, models, profits and samples.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词系在拉丁“份额”上，再让同一观念贯穿比值、设计、选举、处罚、模型、利润与抽样。

normal.en: Split it as pro + portion + al: according to the share. Proportional means the shares stay aligned.
normal.cn: 拆成 pro + portion + al：按份额。proportional 意为份额保持对齐。

normal.en: Picture two water columns rising together: the line between their tops always has the same slope.
normal.cn: 想象两根水柱一起上升：柱顶连线始终是同一条斜线。

normal.en: A proportional model bridge fits in your hand because every length was cut by the same fraction.
normal.cn: 比例模型桥能放进手心，因为每条长度都被同一个分数缩小了。

normal.en: Proportional representation hands out seats in the same fractions as votes.
normal.cn: 比例代表制按与选票相同的分数发放席位。

normal.en: A proportional fine weighs the harm on one pan and the penalty on the other until they balance.
normal.cn: 相称的罚款把损害放在天平一端、处罚放在另一端，直到平衡。

abstract.en: Keep 'proportion' as the noun in mind: proportional is simply the adjective that says the shares agree.
abstract.cn: 心里记住 proportion 是名词：proportional 只是说各份额一致的那个形容词。

abstract.en: Notice the double life: in maths the ratio is exact, in law and design it is judged rather than measured.
abstract.cn: 注意它的双重生活：数学里比值是精确的，法律与设计里则是靠判断而非测量。

abstract.en: Ask 'proportional to what?' Every sense needs a second term: another quantity, a harm, a whole, a population.
abstract.cn: 随时问“与什么成比例？”每个义项都需要第二项：另一个数量、一项损害、一个整体、一个人口。

examples.en: The brightness of a lamp is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
examples.cn: 灯的亮度与距离的平方成反比。

examples.en: The council adopted a proportional system for allocating seats on the new board.
examples.cn: 议会通过了新理事会席位的比例分配制。

examples.en: Analysts expect a proportional rise in shipping costs as fuel prices climb.
examples.cn: 分析师预计运费将随燃料价格上升而成比例上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“扑罗破身呢”：两样东西一起破、一起补，破口大小始终成比例。

root: 拉丁 pro portione“按份额”，portio 意为“份额、分得的部分”，派生 proportio 与 proportionalis；核心是“两份按同一比率增减”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses ask the same question: do the shares still line up? Quantities, columns, seats, penalties, models, profits and samples are proportional when each part keeps the fraction it is supposed to have.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项问的都是同一个问题：各份还对得齐吗？数量、表格列、席位、处罚、模型、利润与样本之所以成比例，是因为每一份都保住了它应有的分数。

core.en: Two or more parts keep a constant relation, so when one changes the others change by the same fraction.
core.cn: 两个或更多部分保持恒定关系，于是一个变化时其余按同一分数变化。

branches.en: QUANTITIES: the ratio between two amounts never shifts.
branches.cn: 数量：两个量之间的比值从不移动。

branches.en: SHAPE: design and models keep every part in its original relation.
branches.cn: 形状：设计与模型让每一部分保持原有关系。

branches.en: ALLOCATION: votes, seats and profits follow the agreed fractions.
branches.cn: 分配：选票、席位与利润遵循约定分数。

branches.en: JUSTICE: the response is weighed against the harm.
branches.cn: 公正：回应与损害放在同一杆秤上衡量。

branches.en: SAMPLING: each subgroup appears in its true share.
branches.cn: 抽样：每个子群按真实份额出现。

intro.en: Proportional is pro + portio + -al. The items below follow the same share noun into adverb, verb, near-synonym and negation.
intro.cn: proportional 由 pro、portio 与 -al 构成。下列条目沿着同一个“份额”名词，走到副词、动词、近义词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the share noun and the phrase that became a noun. They explain why proportion, proportional and proportionate all point back to one allotment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“份额”名词与凝固成名词的短语，解释为什么 proportion、proportional 与 proportionate 都指向同一次分配。

items.meaning: changing in a fixed relation to something else
items.example: The tax is proportional to the value of the land.
items.exampleCN: 税额与土地价值成比例。

items.meaning: a share; the relation between parts
items.meaningCN: 份额；各部分之间的关系
items.example: The proportion of women in the field is rising.
items.exampleCN: 该领域中女性的比例正在上升。

items.example: Costs were shared proportionally among the members.
items.exampleCN: 费用由成员按比例分摊。

items.example: The reply was proportionate to the threat.
items.exampleCN: 这一回应与威胁程度相称。

items.meaning: the quality of being in due proportion
items.example: Lawyers debated the proportionality of the sentence.
items.exampleCN: 律师争论该判决是否相称。

items.meaning: out of proportion; too large or too small
items.meaningCN: 不成比例的；过大或过小的
items.example: The punishment was disproportionate to the error.
items.exampleCN: 这项处罚与过失不相称。

items.structure: proportionate used as a verb form
items.example: Benefits were proportionated to working hours.

items.meaning: able to be brought into proportion
items.meaningCN: 可与之相称的；可成比例的
items.example: The two budgets are proportionable if the scope is cut.
items.exampleCN: 如果削减范围，两份预算可以相称。

definition_zh: 提议；建议；方案；求婚；投标
definition_en: a plan or suggestion offered formally for others to consider; also the act of suggesting, an offer of marriage, or a priced business bid
core_image: 一张写满条目的纸被推到桌子中央，等所有人点头
scene: 会议开到一半，负责预算的人把打印好的方案推到长桌中央，等各部门表态。The finance team submitted a detailed proposal for cutting costs by the end of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 proposal 是「提议、方案」（第 1 个义项：提交讨论的正式计划）；句意为财务团队提交了一份年底前削减成本的详细方案。图中可辨识物件：打印纸、长桌、预算表。

pos.zh: 提议；建议；方案；求婚

derivatives.zh: proposal 去掉后缀 -al 即得动词 propose，义为「提议；求婚」
propose 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -r，义为「提议者；提出者」
与 propose 同出拉丁 proponere，义为「命题；主张；提议」

senses.title: A formal plan put forward for others to consider
senses.definition: a plan or suggestion that is offered formally so that other people can discuss and decide on it
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出、供他人讨论并决定的计划或建议
senses.example: The committee will vote on the housing proposal next week.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会下周将对这份住房方案进行表决。
senses.why: Proposal is propose plus the noun ending -al, so it names the thing that has been placed before people and is waiting for their decision.
senses.whyCN: proposal 是 propose 加名词后缀 -al，因此它指「被摆到众人面前、正等他们决定」的那件东西。

senses.title: An offer of marriage
senses.definition: the act of asking someone to marry you
senses.definitionCN: 请求某人与自己结婚的行为
senses.example: Her answer to his proposal was a quiet yes.
senses.exampleCN: 她对他求婚的回答，是一声轻轻的愿意。
senses.why: A marriage proposal is also something laid before another person; only now the thing offered is a shared future instead of a plan.
senses.whyCN: 求婚同样是把东西摆到对方面前，只是这次献上的不是方案，而是一段共同的未来。

senses.title: The act of suggesting something
senses.definition: the act of putting an idea or suggestion to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把想法或建议提交给某人或某群人的行为
senses.example: The proposal of new safety rules took the whole morning.
senses.exampleCN: 新安全规则的提出花了整整一上午。
senses.why: Because -al can name an action as well as its result, proposal can mean the offering itself, not only the document lying on the table.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -al 既能指动作也能指结果，proposal 便既能指「提出」这个动作本身，也能指桌上那份文件。

senses.title: A formal offer to do work or supply goods
senses.definition: a written offer from a company to do a job or supply goods at a stated price
senses.definitionCN: 公司按标价承接工程或供货的书面报价
senses.example: Three firms sent a proposal for the bridge repair.
senses.exampleCN: 有三家公司为桥梁维修提交了报价书。
senses.why: A business proposal places terms in front of a client, which is the same gesture of putting something forward, now with a price attached.
senses.whyCN: 商务提案是把条件摆到客户面前，与「把东西递上前」是同一个动作，只是这次附上了价格。

intro.en: Proposal is an English noun built from the verb propose and the suffix -al; the verb itself goes back to Latin pro- plus ponere, to place.
intro.cn: proposal 是英语里由动词 propose 加后缀 -al 构成的名词；动词本身可追溯到拉丁语 pro-（向前）加 ponere（放置）。

items.en: Ponere meant to place or set down, and it supplies the core image of putting something in front of someone.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放置、放下」，提供了「把东西摆到某人面前」这一核心意象。

items.en: Pro- meant forward, so proponere meant to put forward, to set before someone, or to offer.
items.cn: pro- 意为「向前」，所以 proponere 意为「摆到前面、呈现给某人、提出」。

items.en: Old French proposer took the Latin verb and meant to suggest or to set out, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 proposer 承袭了这个拉丁动词，意为「建议、陈述」，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: The noun ending -al was added to propose; the silent final e of the verb drops, so propos- plus -al gives proposal.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -al 加在 propose 上，动词末尾不发音的 e 脱落，于是 propos- 加 -al 就是 proposal。

items.en: Modern English uses proposal for plans, for offers of marriage and for priced business bids, while propose stays the verb.
items.cn: 现代英语用 proposal 指方案、求婚与带价的商务报价，而动作仍由动词 propose 承担。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for things offered for acceptance.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示「拿出供人接受之物」的名词。

entries.definition: To suggest a plan, or to ask someone to marry you.
entries.definitionCN: 提出计划，或向某人求婚。

entries.definition: A statement or idea offered for discussion.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供讨论的陈述或主张。

entries.definition: The reason for which something is done; only the spelling looks similar, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的目的；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An idea put forward for someone to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供人考虑的想法。

entries.definition: Something presented to someone for acceptance or refusal.
entries.definitionCN: 呈给某人、供其接受或拒绝的东西。

entries.definition: A formal suggestion made at a meeting for a vote.
entries.definitionCN: 会上提出供表决的正式动议。

entries.definition: A price offered for a job or at an auction.
entries.definitionCN: 为承接工程或在拍卖中出的价。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the verb propose with -al added, and the spelling drops the silent e before the suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是动词 propose 加 -al 而成，加后缀前先去掉不发音的 e。

normal.en: Proposal is propose with the noun ending -al, and the silent final e of propose is dropped before it.
normal.cn: proposal 是 propose 加名词后缀 -al，加之前 propose 末尾不发音的 e 脱落。

normal.en: The Latin verb behind both words is proponere, from pro- forward and ponere to place.
normal.cn: 这两个词背后的拉丁动词是 proponere，由 pro-（向前）与 ponere（放置）组成。

normal.en: A proposal is literally something placed forward, which is why it always faces a reader or a listener.
normal.cn: proposal 字面上就是「被摆到前面的东西」，所以它总是面对某个读者或听者。

normal.en: Marriage proposal uses the same noun because a shared future is also laid before the other person.
normal.cn: marriage proposal 用同一个名词，因为共同的未来也是被摆到对方面前的。

normal.en: Request for proposal is a fixed business phrase for asking firms to send their priced offers.
normal.cn: request for proposal 是固定的商务说法，用来请各公司寄出带价的方案。

abstract.en: The word is a hand pushing a sheet of paper across a table, and every sense keeps that gesture.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一只手把一张纸推过桌面，每个义项都保留着这个动作。

abstract.en: A plan, a marriage and a price are very different things, yet all three are offered by being set in front of someone.
abstract.cn: 方案、婚姻与价格是极不相同的东西，但三者都是靠「摆到对方面前」来献出的。

abstract.en: Because -al names both the act and its result, the same noun can mean the asking and the paper that carries it.
abstract.cn: -al 同时指动作和结果，所以同一个名词既能指「提出」这件事，也能指承载它的那张纸。

examples.en: The board will discuss the proposal tomorrow morning.
examples.cn: 董事会明天上午将讨论这份方案。

examples.en: He got down on one knee for his proposal.
examples.cn: 他单膝跪地求婚。

examples.en: Two suppliers sent a proposal with their prices.
examples.cn: 两家供应商寄来了附有报价的方案。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something placed in front of others; the senses divide into a plan, a marriage offer, the act of suggesting, and a priced bid.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被摆到他人面前的东西」；义项由此分为方案、求婚、提议这一动作，以及带价的投标。

core.cn: 核心意象：一张写好的纸被推到长桌中央，等着众人点头。

branches.cn: 一份削减成本的方案滑过长桌

branches.cn: 三家公司的报价信封先后送到

branches.en: one noun for a private question and a public one
branches.cn: 同一个名词，既指私人的一问，也指公开的提请

definition_zh: 提议；建议；打算；求婚；提名
definition_en: to put forward a plan or idea for others to consider; to ask someone to marry you; to intend to do something; to nominate someone formally
core_image: 一只手把写着想法的纸推到桌面中央，抬头看向众人
scene: 小组讨论卡住时，最年轻的成员把一张草稿推到桌子中间，请大家先看他的思路。She proposed a shorter timetable so that the team could test the design earlier.
sceneCN: 这里 propose 是「提出、提议」（第 1 个义项：把计划或想法提出来供人考虑）；句意为她提出一个更短的时间表，好让团队更早测试设计。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、圆桌、马克杯。

pos.zh: 提议；建议；打算；求婚；提名

derivatives.zh: propose 加名词后缀 -al（末尾 e 脱落），义为「提议；方案；求婚」
propose 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -r，义为「提议者；提出者」

senses.title: To put forward a plan or idea
senses.definition: to suggest a plan, idea, or course of action for other people to consider
senses.definitionCN: 提出计划、想法或行动方案供他人考虑
senses.example: The engineer proposed a cheaper way to reinforce the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师提出了一种更便宜的屋顶加固办法。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to place something in front of someone, so proposing is literally laying an idea on the table for others to look at.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「把东西摆到某人面前」，所以 propose 就是字面意义上的「把想法放到桌面上」让人看。

senses.title: To ask someone to marry you
senses.definition: to ask a person to marry you, usually in a formal or planned way
senses.definitionCN: 请求某人嫁给自己或娶自己，通常正式或经过安排
senses.example: He proposed to her beside the river where they first met.
senses.exampleCN: 他在两人初遇的河边向她求婚。
senses.why: An offer of marriage is placed before the other person like a plan, and the answer comes back as a decision in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 求婚也像一份方案那样摆到对方面前，对方的回答同样是一次决定。

senses.title: To intend or plan to do something (formal)
senses.definition: to intend to do something, especially as a stated plan
senses.definitionCN: 打算做某事，尤指作为已说明的计划
senses.example: The council proposes to close the lane to traffic on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会打算在周日封闭这条小路，禁止车辆通行。
senses.why: What is set before people as a plan also states what the speaker means to do, so the verb comes to mark intention.
senses.whyCN: 摆在众人面前的计划同时也表明了说话人打算做什么，于是这个动词便能标示「意图」。

senses.title: To nominate someone or put a motion formally
senses.definition: to name a person for a position, or to present a motion for a formal vote
senses.definitionCN: 提名某人担任某职，或提出动议交付正式表决
senses.example: She was proposed as the next chair of the society.
senses.exampleCN: 有人提名她担任协会的下一任主席。
senses.why: A name can be placed before a group just as an idea can, so one verb covers nominating a person and moving a motion.
senses.whyCN: 名字和想法一样都能被摆到一群人面前，所以同一个动词既能指提名某人，也能指提出动议。

intro.en: Propose comes from Latin pro- forward and ponere to place, through the French verb proposer; the same stem with the noun ending -al gives proposal.
intro.cn: propose 来自拉丁语 pro-（向前）加 ponere（放置），经法语动词 proposer 进入英语；同一个词干加上名词后缀 -al，就成了 proposal。

items.en: Ponere meant to place, set down, or fix in position, and it is the source of a large family of English words.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放置、放下、固定在某处」，是英语中一大族词的来源。

items.en: With pro- meaning forward, proponere meant to put forward or set before someone, often as an offer.
items.cn: 加上表示「向前」的 pro-，proponere 意为「向前摆出、呈现给某人」，常带「献上」的意味。

items.en: Old French proposer carried the sense of suggesting or setting out, and English took the verb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 proposer 带有「建议、陈述」的意思，英语在十四世纪借入这个动词。

items.en: Modern English propose covers plans, intentions, marriage and nominations, while proposal names the thing offered.
items.cn: 现代英语的 propose 覆盖计划、意图、求婚与提名，而 proposal 指被献出的那个东西。

items.en: Propose ends in a silent e, which drops before the noun ending -al, so propos- plus -al becomes proposal, never proposeal.
items.cn: propose 以不发音的 e 结尾，遇到名词后缀 -al 时这个 e 脱落，于是 propos- 加 -al 写作 proposal，而不会写成 proposeal。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and the Latin relatives of the verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of putting an idea or a name forward.
note.cn: 形近组收这个动词的名词形式与拉丁同族词；近义组收「提出想法或名字」的动词。

entries.definition: To advise that something is a good choice.

normalIntro.en: The verb is built from pro- forward and ponere to place, and its noun keeps the same stem with -al instead of a final e.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词由 pro-（向前）与 ponere（放置）构成，它的名词用同一词干加 -al，而不用末尾的 e。

normal.en: Propose is pro- forward plus ponere to place: to place an idea before people.
normal.cn: propose 是 pro-（向前）加 ponere（放置）：把想法摆到众人面前。

normal.en: Proposal is the same stem with -al, and the e of propose drops, so the noun is spelled propos-al.
normal.cn: proposal 是同一词干加 -al，propose 的 e 脱落，所以名词拼作 propos-al。

normal.en: Propose a toast and propose a plan use the same gesture of holding something out to others.
normal.cn: propose a toast 与 propose a plan 用的是同一个「把东西端给别人」的动作。

normal.en: Propose to someone keeps the offer image, with a shared life as the thing offered.
normal.cn: propose to someone 保留了「献上」的意象，只是献出的东西变成共同的生活。

normal.en: Propose a motion and propose a candidate both put a wording or a name in front of a group for a vote.
normal.cn: propose a motion 与 propose a candidate 都是把一段文字或一个名字摆到一群人面前等待表决。

abstract.en: The verb is an open hand: whatever it offers must be visible to the people who will decide.
abstract.cn: 这个动词就是一只摊开的手：它献出的东西必须让将要决定的人看得见。

abstract.en: A plan, a marriage and a name all travel the same path, from a private thought to a public table.
abstract.cn: 计划、婚姻与名字走的是同一条路：从私下的念头，到公开的桌面上。

abstract.en: The missing e in proposal is the trace of the verb handing its meaning over to the noun.
abstract.cn: proposal 里少掉的那个 e，正是动词把意义交给名词时留下的痕迹。

examples.en: The city proposed a new bike lane along the river.
examples.cn: 市里提议沿河修一条新的自行车道。

examples.en: He proposed to her after dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭后，他向她求婚。

examples.en: They propose to move the office closer to the station.

senses.title: Criminal proceedings against an accused
senses.titleCN: 对被告的刑事起诉程序
senses.definition: the process of charging someone and pursuing the case in court
senses.definitionCN: 对某人提出指控并在法院推进案件的过程
senses.example: The prosecution began as soon as the evidence file reached the state's lawyers.
senses.exampleCN: 证据卷一交到州律师手中，公诉程序就开始了。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to follow forward, and the legal noun pictures the state following a charge through every stage of a trial.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向前追随」，这个法律名词描绘的正是国家把一项指控追随到审判的每一个阶段。

senses.title: The prosecuting authority
senses.definition: the body or office that has the power to bring charges
senses.definitionCN: 有权提出刑事指控的机构或部门
senses.example: The prosecution decided not to pursue the minor charge.
senses.exampleCN: 检察机关决定不追究那项轻微的指控。
senses.why: An institution can stand for the act it performs, so the abstract noun also names the office that decides whether to charge.
senses.whyCN: 机构可以代表它所做的动作，所以这个抽象名词也指决定是否起诉的那个部门。

senses.title: The state's lawyers in court
senses.definition: the lawyers presenting the state's case in a particular trial
senses.definitionCN: 在具体审判中代表国家陈述案件的律师
senses.example: The prosecution sat on the left and the defence on the right.
senses.exampleCN: 控方坐在左边，辩方坐在右边。
senses.why: In courtroom speech the abstract noun becomes a collective label for the legal team on the charging side, like defence on the other side.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭用语里，这个抽象名词变成指控一侧律师团队的集体标签，正如另一侧被称为辩方。

senses.title: The decision to lay charges
senses.definition: the moment or act of formally charging a person
senses.definitionCN: 正式对某人提出指控的那一动作或时刻
senses.example: A prosecution at this stage would need stronger evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个阶段起诉，需要更有力的证据。
senses.why: The word covers the beginning as well as the whole case, because a charge is both a single decision and a long proceeding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既覆盖开端，也覆盖整个案件，因为一次指控既是一个决定，也是一段漫长的程序。

senses.title: Formal carrying out of a task
senses.titleCN: 正式从事、推行某项工作
senses.definition: in formal writing, the carrying out or pursuit of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中，指对某项活动的推行与从事
senses.example: He was praised for the prosecution of his duties during the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 他因危机期间尽责履职而受到赞扬。
senses.why: The old sense of following something forward survives in formal prose, where any duty or study can be prosecuted, not only a crime.
senses.whyCN: 「把某事向前推进」的旧义在正式文字中保留下来：任何职责或研究都可以被「推行」，并不限于罪行。

senses.title: Pursuit or continuation of an undertaking
senses.titleCN: 事业或行动的继续推进
senses.definition: in older usage, the continued pursuit of a war, a policy or a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，对战争、政策或计划的持续推进
senses.example: The history devotes a chapter to the prosecution of the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这部史书用一章讲战争的进行。
senses.why: Before the word narrowed to law, it named any energetic continuation, and military and political writing kept that wider reach.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词收窄到法律之前，它指任何有力的持续推进，军事与政治文字保留了这一较宽的范围。

senses.title: The evidence stage of a trial
senses.definition: the part of a trial in which the charging side presents its evidence
senses.definitionCN: 审判中由指控方出示证据的那一部分
senses.example: During the prosecution, three experts described the damaged wall.
senses.exampleCN: 在控方举证阶段，三位专家描述了受损的墙体。
senses.why: Since the state speaks first, its phase of the trial takes the name of the whole proceeding, a part standing for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 因为国家一方先发言，审判中属于它的那个阶段便取了整个程序的名字，以部分代整体。

senses.title: Pursuit of a claim in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中对请求的追究
senses.definition: in older legal writing, the pursuing of any claim or suit
senses.definitionCN: 在较早法律文字中，对任何请求或诉讼的追究
senses.example: The record notes the prosecution of a debt against the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 档案记载了对该遗产的一笔债务追索。
senses.why: Civil claims were once prosecuted as well as criminal charges, and older documents use the noun for any claim pursued to judgment.
senses.whyCN: 民事请求一度与刑事指控一样被「追究」，较早文书便用这个名词指任何追究至判决的请求。

intro.en: Prosecution comes from Latin prosecutio, the noun of prosequi 'to follow forward', built from pro- 'forth' plus sequi 'to follow'. The oldest sense is continuation, and law narrowed it to the pursuit of a charge.
intro.cn: prosecution 来自拉丁 prosecutio，即 prosequi「向前追随」的名词，由 pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成。最古老的含义是「继续」，法律把它收窄为对指控的追究。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow. It also stands behind sequence, consecutive and the second half of prosecute, showing how widely the idea of following spread.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随。它也是 sequence、consecutive 以及 prosecute 后半的来源，可见「跟随」这一观念散布之广。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi gave prosequi, 'to follow forward, to pursue, to continue'. In legal use it meant to pursue a charge or a claim.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi 构成 prosequi，意为向前追随、追求、继续。在法律用法中指追究一项指控或请求。

items.en: The noun prosecutio named the following or the pursuing, and could describe the continuation of any undertaking, not only a legal one.
items.cn: 名词 prosecutio 指追随或追究，可描述任何事业的继续，而不仅限于法律事务。

items.en: French legal usage applied the noun to the conduct of a case, and English borrowed it with that narrower focus already attached.
items.cn: 法语法律用法把这个名词用于案件进行，英语借入时已带着这一较窄的侧重。

items.en: English used prosecution for both the conduct of a criminal case and the carrying on of any business, keeping the two senses side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 英语用 prosecution 既指刑事案件的进行，也指任何事务的推行，两个含义并行了数百年。

items.en: Modern English centres the word on criminal proceedings, while the 'carrying out' sense survives in formal phrases about duties, studies or a war.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词的中心放在刑事程序上，而「推行」义保存在关于职责、研究或战争的正式说法里。

note.en: Group one separates the related verb and agent from a near look-alike with a hostile prefix and from a word that only shares spelling; group two sets the proceeding against the other names for a case.
note.cn: 第一组区分同根动词与施事者、一个带敌对前缀的形近词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；第二组把这个程序与案件的其他名目作对照。

entries.definition: To bring and conduct the case; prosecution is the proceeding as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指提起并推进案件；prosecution 指整个程序。

entries.definition: The lawyer who conducts the case; the prosecution can also mean the team or the proceeding.
entries.definitionCN: 指推进案件的律师；prosecution 也可指团队或程序。

entries.definition: Systematic mistreatment, from per- 'through' plus the same following verb; the prefix makes it harassment, not litigation.
entries.definitionCN: 系统性迫害，由 per-「贯穿」加同一个「跟随」动词构成；前缀使它成为迫害，而不是诉讼。

entries.definition: A ban or outlawry, from proscribere 'to write up publicly'; it shares the opening letters but not the following verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指禁令或剥夺公权，来自 proscribere「公开书写」；它与本词只共享开头字母，并不共享「跟随」动词。

entries.definition: Relating to a prosecutor or the conduct of a prosecution, not the proceeding itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指与检察官或起诉行为有关的，不是程序本身。

entries.definition: The court hearing where evidence is tested; prosecution is the pursuing of the charge, which may end before trial.
entries.definitionCN: 指检验证据的庭审；prosecution 指对指控的追究，可能在开庭前就结束。

entries.definition: The whole matter before a court, civil or criminal; prosecution belongs to the criminal side.
entries.definitionCN: 指提交法院的整个事项，民事刑事皆可；prosecution 属刑事一侧。

entries.definition: The formal steps of a legal action; prosecution is the state's pursuit of a charge within them.
entries.definitionCN: 指法律行动的一系列正式步骤；prosecution 是其中对指控的国家追究。

entries.definition: The formal accusation itself, often after a grand jury; prosecution is the process that follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式指控文书本身，常在大陪审团之后；prosecution 是随后展开的程序。

entries.definition: A lawsuit in civil law or a military engagement; in legal speech it is broader and often civil.
entries.definitionCN: 指民事法中的诉讼，或军事行动；在法律用语中范围更广，且常指民事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real following verb, the real hostile prefix and the real procedural pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「跟随」动词、真实的敌对前缀，以及真实的程序配对。

normal.en: Prosequi is to follow forward: the state follows its charge from filing to verdict.
normal.cn: prosequi 是向前追：国家把指控从立案一路跟到判决。

normal.en: Persecution has the same following verb but a prefix of 'through': one follows to court, the other follows to harm.
normal.cn: persecution 共享「跟随」动词，但前缀意为「贯穿」：一个跟到法院，一个跟到伤害。

normal.en: Proscription is a look-alike about public writing, not about following.
normal.cn: proscription 是形近词，讲的是公开书写，而不是跟随。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: the prosecution and the defence, charging side and answering side.
normal.cn: 这组配对是固定的：控方与辩方，指控一侧与答辩一侧。

normal.en: The family runs prosecute, prosecution, prosecutor and prosecutorial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 prosecute、prosecution、prosecutor、prosecutorial。

abstract.en: Picture evidence bags laid end to end, forming a path toward an empty chair.
abstract.cn: 想象证据袋首尾相接，铺成一条通向空椅子的路。

abstract.en: Picture a charge as a rope that the state keeps pulling, hand over hand, through every hearing.
abstract.cn: 想象指控是一根绳，国家一场庭审接一场庭审地双手交替往回拉。

abstract.en: Picture one side of a courtroom speaking first because the state is the one that complains.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭一侧先开口，因为提出申诉的是国家。

examples.en: The prosecution rested after four days of testimony.
examples.cn: 经过四天作证，控方结束了举证。

examples.en: Without the second witness, the prosecution would probably fail.
examples.cn: 若没有第二位证人，这场起诉很可能失败。

examples.en: He wrote a book on the prosecution of long wars.
examples.cn: 他写了一本关于长期战争如何进行的书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖诉究神」——把诉状层层剖开、一路追到底 → 起诉、检控

root: 拉丁 prosequi（向前追随、追究）的名词 prosecutio，由 pro-（向前）加 sequi（跟随）构成；古义为「继续、推行」，后收窄为「起诉」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the criminal proceeding, through the authority, the courtroom team, the laying of charges, formal carrying out, the older continuation of an undertaking, the evidence stage, and the old pursuit of a claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从刑事程序开始，经检察机关、庭上的控方团队、提起指控、正式推行工作、旧时对事业的继续、举证阶段，最后到旧时对请求的追究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: evidence bags laid end to end toward an empty chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：证据袋首尾相接，铺向一把空椅子。

branches.en: THE PROCEEDING: the state follows its charge through every stage of court.
branches.cn: 程序：国家把指控追随到法院的每一个阶段。

branches.en: THE THREE FACES: the authority, the team in court and the single decision to charge are one system seen at different distances.
branches.cn: 三张面孔：检察机关、庭上团队与提出指控的那一个决定，是同一系统在不同距离下的样子。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: any duty, study or war can be carried forward, which is what the verb meant before law took it over.
branches.cn: 旧义：任何职责、研究或战争都能被推行，这正是法律接管这个词之前它的意思。

branches.en: THE HEARING: the side that speaks first gives its name to the evidence stage.
branches.cn: 庭审：先发言的一侧把自己的名字给了举证阶段。

branches.en: THE WIDER CLAIM: older documents also prosecute debts and civil claims, not only crimes.
branches.cn: 更宽的请求：较早文书也「追究」债务与民事请求，并不限于罪行。

intro.en: Prosecution is a Latin action noun built on a verb of following, so it names a process rather than a person.
intro.cn: prosecution 是建立在「跟随」动词上的拉丁动作名词，所以它命名的是过程，而不是人。

latinIntro.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi 'follow' gives prosequi; the participle prosecutus and the noun prosecutio supply the stem, and -tion makes the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成 prosequi；分词 prosecutus 与名词 prosecutio 提供词干，-tion 构成英语名词。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「跟随」指向前方。

items.meaningCN: 动作或过程（名词后缀把动词转成程序名）
items.example: The suffix made a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成过程名词。

items.meaningCN: 对指控的追究（由动作转为整套程序）
推进案件的施事者（施事后缀把过程转成人）

items.meaning: to bring and conduct a case

与检察官有关的（形容词后缀把角色转成属性）

sceneCN: 这里 prospect 是「可能性、机会」（第 2 个义项：某事将会发生或成功的可能性）；句意：这里找到铜的可能性很大，但他宁愿过安稳日子。画面里有山脊、晨雾和尚未开挖的谷地；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The future in view: what lies ahead
senses.titleCN: 前景：前方等待的那幅图景
senses.definition: the possibility or expectation of something happening in the future, especially something good
senses.definitionCN: 对未来某事的可能性或预期，尤指好事
senses.example: The prospect of a long winter worried the farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长冬季的前景让农民们忧心。
senses.why: The noun appears in the 1660s as 'expectation, ground of expectation', from the habit of looking forward. What the eye does in space, the mind does in time: it scans the horizon of coming events.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在 17 世纪 60 年代出现，义为“预期、期待的依据”，来自“向前看”的动作。眼睛在空间里做的事，心智在时间里也做：它扫视将要发生之事的地平线。

senses.title: A chance that may come true
senses.titleCN: 可能性、机会：尚未兑现的那份可能
senses.definition: a chance or possibility that something will happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 某事将会发生或成功的可能性
senses.example: There is little prospect of finding survivors after so long.
senses.exampleCN: 过了这么久，找到幸存者的可能性很小。
senses.why: The 1620s sense 'mental view or survey' let people speak of viewing a future outcome. Once an outcome is 'in view', it is a chance on the horizon rather than a certainty in hand.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代“心中的审视”这一义项，让人可以“看见”未来的结果。一个结果一旦“在视野里”，它就是地平线上的机会，而不是握在手里的确定。

senses.title: The sweep of the eye: a wide view
senses.titleCN: 景象、视野：眼睛扫过的那一大片
senses.definition: a view or scene, especially a wide one seen from a high place
senses.definitionCN: 景色、景象，尤指从高处看到的广阔视野
senses.example: From the hilltop we had a fine prospect of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 从山顶上，我们看到了山谷的美丽景色。
senses.why: From 1530s English, prospect meant 'extensive view of the landscape', straight from Latin prospectus 'distant view'. The word still carries the physical sweep of the eye before it carries hope.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪 30 年代起，prospect 指“广阔的风景视野”，直接来自拉丁语 prospectus“远处的景色”。这个词先有眼睛的物理扫视，后才有希望之义。

senses.title: Someone worth watching: the promising person
senses.titleCN: 潜在客户、有前途的人选：值得盯住的那个人
senses.definition: a person or thing seen as likely to succeed, or a possible customer or candidate
senses.definitionCN: 被认为可能成功的人或事物；潜在客户或候选人
senses.example: The agent spends her mornings calling new prospects.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经纪人每天上午给新潜在客户打电话。
senses.why: From 1922, prospect named 'a person or thing considered promising', out of the 1660s sense of expectation of advantage. A good customer is someone in whom the seller sees a future.
senses.whyCN: 从 1922 年起，prospect 指“被认为有前途的人或事物”，源自 17 世纪 60 年代“预期好处”的义项。好客户，就是卖方在其身上看得见未来的人。

senses.title: Grounds for hoping
senses.titleCN: 预期的依据：凭什么盼着
senses.definition: grounds for expecting something; a reasonable basis for anticipation
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的预期依据；合理的盼望理由
senses.example: The deal offers no prospect of profit this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易今年没有获利的指望。
senses.why: The 1660s sense was not the hope itself but its ground: 'expectation, ground of expectation'. The landscape metaphor persists — a prospect is what the situation lets you see coming.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 60 年代的义项不是希望本身，而是希望的依据：“预期、期待的依据”。风景的隐喻仍在：prospect 就是局势允许你看见的、即将到来的东西。

senses.title: Looking for ore: to prospect the ground
senses.definition: to search an area for gold, oil, or other minerals
senses.definitionCN: 在某地区寻找黄金、石油或其他矿藏
senses.example: They prospected the valley for copper throughout the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天他们都在那个山谷里勘探铜矿。
senses.why: The verb dates from 1841, from a specialized 1832 noun sense 'a spot giving prospects of ore'. The miner literally looks out over the land to see what it promises.
senses.whyCN: 动词始于 1841 年，来自 1832 年的名词专义“有矿苗的地方”。矿工字面上就是在土地上四处张望，看它许诺了什么。

senses.title: Surveying the site before building
senses.titleCN: 勘察、探测：动工之前先看一遍
senses.definition: to examine land or a site, especially to judge its potential or value
senses.definitionCN: 勘查土地或场地，尤指评估其潜力或价值
senses.example: Engineers prospected the site before the dam was approved.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝获批之前，工程师们勘察了坝址。
senses.why: English had an older verb prospect 'look forth, look out over' (1550s) from Latin prospectare, a frequentative of prospicere. The mining sense revived that old surveying gesture.
senses.whyCN: 英语早有动词 prospect“向外看、俯瞰”（16 世纪 50 年代），来自拉丁语 prospectare，是 prospicere 的反复体。采矿义让这个古老的勘看动作重新流行。

senses.title: A mental survey: the wide view of a subject
senses.titleCN: 宏观审视：把一门学问摊开来看
senses.definition: a broad mental view or survey of a subject, situation, or period
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题、局势或时期的宏观心理审视
senses.example: The book gives a broad prospect of a century of science.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对百年科学史作了宏观的审视。
senses.why: The transferred sense 'mental view or survey' is recorded from the 1620s. The eye's sweep over a valley becomes the mind's sweep over a field of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: “心中的视野/审视”这一转移义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代。眼睛扫过山谷的动作，变成了心智扫过一片知识领域。

senses.title: The long straight avenue
senses.titleCN: 大街、大道：一眼望不到头的那条路
senses.definition: a wide, straight street or avenue, especially in a Russian city
senses.definitionCN: 宽阔笔直的大街或大道，尤指俄罗斯城市中的
senses.example: Nevsky Prospect runs straight through the heart of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 涅瓦大街笔直地穿过城市中心。
senses.why: In 1866 English borrowed Russian prospekt 'avenue', which itself came from Latin prospectus. A grand avenue is a street designed to give the eye a long, uninterrupted prospect.
senses.whyCN: 1866 年英语借入俄语 prospekt“大街”，而俄语这个词又来自拉丁语 prospectus。宏伟的大道，就是一条为了让视线获得漫长而不中断的前景而设计的街。

intro.en: Prospect is one of the spec- words: all of them are about looking. Latin prospicere 'look forward' gives the noun prospectus 'a distant view', and English extends the same word from landscape to expectation, to customers, and finally to mining.
intro.cn: prospect 是 spec- 词族的一员：它们都与“看”有关。拉丁语 prospicere“向前看”给出名词 prospectus“远处的景色”，英语再把同一个词从风景扩展到预期、客户，最后扩展到采矿。

items.en: Prospicere meant 'to look out on, look forward', built from pro 'forward' plus specere 'to look at'. Specere goes back to PIE *spek- 'to observe', a reconstruction with no written record, so that deepest layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: prospicere 意为“眺望、向前看”，由 pro“向前”加 specere“看”构成。specere 可追溯到印欧语 *spek-“观察”，但这是没有书面记录的重构，因此最深层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Prospectus, the past-participle stem used as a noun, meant 'distant view, look out; sight, faculty of sight'. It named both the thing seen and the power of seeing it.
items.cn: prospectus 由过去分词词干用作名词，意为“远处的景色、眺望；视觉、视力”。它既指被看见之物，也指看见的能力。

items.en: The noun enters English as 'the act of looking into the distance; the condition of facing something or a certain direction'. The looking is still literal.
items.cn: 名词进入英语时意为“向远处看的动作；朝向某物或某个方向的状态”。这里的“看”仍是字面义。

items.en: The meaning widens to 'an extensive view of the landscape' (1530s), then to 'mental view or survey' (1620s), then to 'that which is presented to the eye, a scene' (1630s).
items.cn: 词义先扩展为“广阔的风景视野”（16 世纪 30 年代），再扩展为“心中的审视”（17 世纪 20 年代），又扩展为“呈现于眼前之物、景象”（17 世纪 30 年代）。

items.en: 'Expectation, ground of expectation, especially of advantage' appears in the 1660s on the notion of looking forward. From it come 'person or thing considered promising' (1922) and the plural prospects, 'things looked forward to'.
items.cn: “预期、期待的依据，尤指好处”于 17 世纪 60 年代出现，基于“向前看”的意象。由此派生出“被认为有前途的人或事物”（1922）以及复数 prospects“所期待之事”。

items.en: Mining uses a specialized noun sense 'a spot giving prospects of ore' (1832), and the verb 'explore for gold or minerals' follows in 1841, from prospect (n.).
items.cn: 采矿业先有名词专义“有矿苗的地点”（1832），动词“勘探黄金或矿物”于 1841 年随后出现，来自名词 prospect。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spec- look or the -spect shape; the meaning group shares the idea of a future chance, but not its spelling.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spec-“看”或 -spect 的外形；近义组共享“未来的机会”这一概念，但拼写不同。

entries.definition: a printed plan describing a school, company, or proposed enterprise. It is prospect plus the Latin noun ending -us.
entries.definitionCN: 介绍学校、公司或拟办事业的印刷章程。它就是 prospect 加上拉丁名词词尾 -us。

entries.definition: to look back at someone with esteem. It uses the same specere 'look' but with re- 'back'.
entries.definitionCN: 尊重；回头看某人并怀有敬意。它用同一个 specere“看”，但前缀是 re-“向后”。

entries.definition: a person who watches an event. The root is pure 'look', with no pro- 'forward'.
entries.definitionCN: 观众；旁观者。词根是纯粹的“看”，没有 pro-“向前”。

entries.definition: a way of seeing things from a particular point. It looks through a situation rather than forward.
entries.definitionCN: 视角；透视法。它是透过一个情境去看，而不是向前看。

entries.definition: the likely future of a situation. It is the closest everyday synonym of prospect in the sense of expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 前景；展望。在“预期”这一义项上，它是最接近 prospect 的日常同义词。

entries.definition: the chance that something will happen. It measures probability, while prospect often adds hope or dread.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性；或然性。它衡量概率，而 prospect 常带有希望或忧虑的色彩。

entries.definition: a long, wide view, especially between rows of trees. It matches the landscape sense of prospect.
entries.definitionCN: 远景；狭长的视野，尤指树列之间的。它对应 prospect 的风景义。

entries.definition: the act of expecting something and preparing for it. It names the mental act that prospect describes as a view.
entries.definitionCN: 预期；期待。它命名的是 prospect 以“视野”来描绘的那种心理活动。

entries.definition: something that may exist or happen. It is neutral, where prospect usually implies evaluation.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性；可能之事。它是中性的，而 prospect 通常含有评价意味。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin specere 'to look', the spec- family, and the mining and customer senses that grew from the same gaze.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 specere“看”、spec- 词族，以及从同一道目光里长出的采矿义和客户义。

normal.en: prospect = pro- 'forward' + spect 'look': to look forward is to see a prospect.
normal.cn: prospect = pro-“向前”+ spect“看”：向前看，看见的就是前景。

normal.en: The spec- family is all eyes: spectator, inspect, respect, perspective, circumspect.
normal.cn: spec- 词族全是眼睛：spectator、inspect、respect、perspective、circumspect。

normal.en: A prospectus is the same word in a brochure: a school lets you look ahead at what it offers.
normal.cn: prospectus 就是同一个词做成的小册子：学校让你提前看见它能提供什么。

normal.en: A prospector looks over the ground exactly as you look over the future.
normal.cn: prospector（勘探者）打量土地的样子，正像你打量未来。

normal.en: Job prospects are literally 'things looked forward to' in the plural.
normal.cn: job prospects 字面上就是复数形式的“被向前看的事情”。

abstract.en: Future is treated as a landscape: you stand here and scan what is coming.
abstract.cn: 未来被当作一片风景：你站在此处，扫视将要到来的一切。

abstract.en: Looking and hoping are one gesture in this word; the eye and the mind share a horizon.
abstract.cn: 在这个词里，看与盼是同一个动作；眼睛和心智共享一条地平线。

abstract.en: The word travels from landscape to time to market: a view, a chance, a customer.
abstract.cn: 这个词从风景走到时间，再走到市场：一片景、一个机会、一位客户。

examples.en: The prospect of moving abroad excited her more than it frightened her.
examples.cn: 移居国外的前景让她兴奋多过害怕。

examples.en: Geologists spent three years prospecting for oil in the desert.
examples.cn: 地质学家在沙漠里花了三年勘探石油。

examples.en: The sales team treats every inquiry as a potential prospect.
examples.cn: 销售团队把每一次询价都当作潜在客户。

dict_mnemonic.text: pro（向前）+ spect（看）——向前看，前景就在眼前；谐音“普罗斯佩克特”：普查（pro）一遍，向前看矿藏 → prospect 前景；勘探

root: 源自拉丁语 prospicere“向前看、眺望”，由 pro“向前”加 specere“看”构成，名词 prospectus 意为“远处的景色”；核心是“向前看所得到的那片景”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one gaze. The eye first sweeps a landscape, then the mind sweeps the future; what is seen becomes a chance, a customer, a subject surveyed, a street, and finally ground to be searched for ore.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一道目光。眼睛先扫过风景，心智再扫过未来；被看见的东西依次变成机会、客户、被审视的学科、一条大街，最后成为要去地下搜寻矿藏的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing high and looking forward — the view ahead, in space or in time.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在高处向前看——空间或时间中前方的那片景。

chain: SEE A CHANCE IN A PERSON

branches.en: THE EXPECTED FUTURE: prospect as what is anticipated, and the grounds for that anticipation.
branches.cn: 被期待的未来：作为预期内容的前景，以及支撑这份预期的依据。

branches.en: THE CHANCE AND THE PERSON: a possibility on the horizon, and someone in whom a future is seen.
branches.cn: 机会与人：地平线上的可能性，以及被人看见未来的人。

branches.en: THE WIDE VIEW: the landscape before the eyes, and the broad survey before the mind.
branches.cn: 广阔视野：眼前的风景，以及心智对学科的宏观审视。

branches.en: LOOKING INTO THE EARTH: mining for ore, and surveying a site for what it may yield.
branches.cn: 向地下看：探矿，以及为评估潜力而勘察场地。

branches.en: THE LONG AVENUE: a street built to give the eye an unbroken prospect.
branches.cn: 长长的大道：一条为了让视线获得不中断前景而建的街。

intro.en: Prospect is pro- plus spec- plus -t. Its family shows the prefix pro-, re-, per-, circum- and in-, the root spec- 'look', and the noun and agent endings -tus, -tor, -ive and -ion.
intro.cn: prospect 是 pro- 加 spec- 再加 -t。它的词族展示前缀 pro-、re-、per-、circum-、in-，词根 spec-“看”，以及名词与施事后缀 -tus、-tor、-ive、-ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere 'to look at' is the base of spectator, inspect and respect; with prefixes it yields prospicere, respicere, perspicere and circumspicere, and the noun prospectus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere“看”是 spectator、inspect、respect 的基础；加前缀又给出 prospicere、respicere、perspicere、circumspicere，以及名词 prospectus。

items.meaning: a view ahead; expectation; to search the ground
items.example: The prospect of promotion kept her working late.
items.exampleCN: 升职的前景让她一直工作到很晚。

items.example: Officials came to inspect the factory.
items.exampleCN: 官员们来检查这家工厂。

items.meaning: to look back at with esteem
items.example: Students respect a teacher who listens.
items.exampleCN: 学生尊敬愿意倾听的老师。

items.example: The stadium held fifty thousand spectators.
items.exampleCN: 体育场容纳了五万名观众。

items.meaning: a way of seeing through a scene
items.example: Travel gives you a new perspective on home.
items.exampleCN: 旅行让你对家乡有了新的视角。

items.meaning: to look out mentally; to guess or invest
items.example: Reporters speculated about the reason for her resignation.
items.exampleCN: 记者们推测她辞职的原因。

items.meaning: the side something presents to the eye
items.meaningCN: 方面；外观（看过去的那一面）
items.example: We discussed every aspect of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 我们讨论了计划的每个方面。

items.meaningCN: 谨慎的（四周看遍再行动）
items.example: She was circumspect in accepting the offer.
items.exampleCN: 她在接受这个提议时很谨慎。

items.meaning: looking inward at one's own mind
items.example: His diary is a record of quiet introspection.
items.exampleCN: 他的日记是一份安静内省的记录。

items.meaning: a printed plan that lets you look ahead
items.meaningCN: 章程；招股书（让人预先看清全貌）
items.example: The university's prospectus lists every course.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学的章程列出了每一门课程。

latinEntries.meaning: to look forward, look out on

definition_zh: 繁荣；兴旺；成功；富足；顺境
definition_en: the condition of being successful and growing, especially when a country, region or business has rising income, trade and well-being
core_image: 粮仓一格格装满，账本上的数字连年往上走
scene: 港口重新修好的那几年，小城的码头上又挤满了货船，店铺一家接一家开张。In the years after the harbour was rebuilt, prosperity returned to the little town.
sceneCN: 这里 prosperity 表示「经济繁荣、兴旺」（第 1 个义项：地区经济向上走）；句意为港口重建后的几年里，繁荣又回到了这座小城。

pos.zh: 繁荣；兴旺；成功；顺境

derivatives.zh: prosper 加 -ous 构成形容词，把「兴旺」写成一种性质
去掉后缀即得动词，意为「兴旺、发达」
prosperous 再加 -ly 构成副词，意为「兴旺地、富足地」

senses.title: Economic success and growth
senses.definition: the condition in which a country or region grows richer, with rising trade, income and employment
senses.definitionCN: 国家或地区越来越富裕，贸易、收入与就业都在上升的状态
senses.example: The port brought prosperity to the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 这座港口给整个地区带来了繁荣。
senses.why: Prosperity first names the visible sign of a hope that came true: warehouses full, ships coming in, wages paid. Because the Latin stem joins a forward direction to hope, the word naturally settles on growth you can see in a harbour or a market.
senses.whyCN: prosperity 最初指的是希望兑现之后看得见的迹象：仓库堆满、船只进港、工钱按时发放。它的拉丁词干把「朝前」和「希望」绑在一起，所以这个词自然落在港口与市场上看得见的增长。

senses.title: Personal success and good fortune
senses.definition: the state of doing well in one's life or career, with things going favourably
senses.definitionCN: 在人生或事业上走得顺，事情朝着有利方向发展的状态
senses.example: He attributed his prosperity to patience and a little luck.
senses.exampleCN: 他把自己的成功归功于耐心和一点运气。
senses.why: A hope placed in front of a country can also be placed in front of one person: when plans keep working out, the same word names a private run of good years rather than a national boom.
senses.whyCN: 放在一个国家前面的希望，也能放在一个人前面：当计划一件件走通，同一个词就从国家层面的景气转到私人生活里的一段好年景。

senses.title: A period of thriving
senses.definition: a stretch of years in which business and living standards are strong, seen as a period one can date
senses.definitionCN: 生意与生活水平都很强劲的一段年头，可以被标出起止时间
senses.example: The decades of prosperity ended abruptly with the war.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年的繁荣随着战争戛然而止。
senses.why: A boom has a beginning and an end, so the word can be counted and dated; it then names the years themselves, not a permanent condition.
senses.whyCN: 景气有开头也有结尾，所以这个词可以被计数、被标出年份；这时它指的是那几年本身，而不是一种永久状态。

senses.title: Material wealth; affluence
senses.definition: great wealth, especially as shown in comfortable living conditions and possessions
senses.definitionCN: 大量财富，尤指体现在舒适生活条件与财物上的富足
senses.example: They lived in prosperity, but never talked about money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们日子过得很富足，却从不谈钱。
senses.why: Seen through a household rather than a nation, the same state turns into furniture, food and leisure, so the word comes to mean the wealth itself rather than the growth that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 若从一户人家而不是一个国家的角度去看，同一种状态就变成家具、饭菜与闲暇，于是这个词指的是财富本身，而不是产生财富的那段增长。

senses.title: Favourable conditions; good fortune
senses.definition: favourable circumstances or good luck, especially in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 有利的境况或好运气，多见于较早或文学性的用法
senses.example: He wished them health and prosperity in the coming year.
senses.exampleCN: 他祝他们来年健康顺遂。
senses.why: Before economics took the word over, it covered any favourable turn of events; the old blessing formula keeps that wider sense alive in toasts and greetings.
senses.whyCN: 在经济学接管这个词之前，它泛指任何有利的转折；祝酒与贺词里那套古老的祝福语，把这层更宽的意味保留了下来。

intro.en: Prosperity comes from Latin prosperitas, a noun built on prosperus, which is usually analysed as pro- 'forward' plus spes 'hope'.
intro.cn: prosperity 来自拉丁语 prosperitas，其基础是 prosperus；一般认为它由 pro-「向前」加 spes「希望」构成。

items.en: Spes meant hope. The picture behind it is a hope set in front of a person, something to walk toward.
items.cn: spes 意为希望。它背后的画面是把希望摆在人的前面，让人朝它走去。

items.en: Pro- (forward) plus spes gave prosperus, 'favourable, fortunate'. This is the usual analysis; the exact formation is still debated.
items.cn: pro-（向前）加 spes 得到 prosperus，意为「顺利的、吉利的」。这是通常的分析，但具体构词细节仍有讨论。

items.en: Prosperitas named favourable fortune and success, the abstract state behind the adjective.
items.cn: prosperitas 指顺遂的运气与成功，是把那个形容词变成抽象状态的名称。

items.en: Old French passed the noun on as prosperite, meaning success and well-being, and English took it in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词写作 prosperite，意为成功与安好，英语在十五世纪借入。

items.en: Modern English prosperity covers national economies, private wealth and any run of good years.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prosperity 覆盖国家经济、私人财富以及任何一段顺遂的年头。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin family around spes; the near-meaning group collects words for wealth and growth.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 spes 这一拉丁词族展开；近义组收表示财富与增长的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective built on the same stem, describing someone or something that is doing well.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的形容词，形容人或事物兴旺、发达。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to succeed or to do well, the base of both the noun and the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为兴旺、发达，是名词与形容词共同的词干。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a successful or wealthy way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为兴旺地、富足地。

entries.definition: A rare noun for the quality of being prosperous.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的名词，指兴旺、富足的性质。

entries.definition: A large amount of money and possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 大量钱财与财物；财富。

entries.definition: A period when trade and business grow quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 商业迅速增长的时期；景气。

entries.definition: The state of having plenty of money and comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财与舒适生活的状态；富足。

entries.definition: The achievement of a goal, or of fame and money.
entries.definitionCN: 达到目标，或获得名声与财富；成功。

normalIntro.en: Most of the word is carried by two Latin pieces, pro- and spes, and by the English suffixes that turn the verb prosper into a state.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词大半由两个拉丁成分撑起：pro- 与 spes，再加上把动词 prosper 变成状态名词的英语后缀。

normal.en: Pro- means forward and spes means hope, so prosperity is hope that has moved in front of you and come true.
normal.cn: pro- 是向前，spes 是希望，所以 prosperity 是「被放到你前面并且兑现了的希望」。

normal.en: Prosper is the verb underneath: a person prospers, and prosperity is the state that results.
normal.cn: 底下的动词是 prosper：人先兴旺起来，prosperity 是随之而来的状态。

normal.en: The suffix -ity turns an adjective into a state, the same way able becomes ability.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ity 把形容词变成状态，就像 able 变成 ability 一样。

normal.en: The Latin hope word spes also hides in desperate, where de- means without, so desperate is literally 'without hope'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语的希望 spes 还藏在 desperate 里：de- 表示「没有」，desperate 字面就是「没有希望」。

normal.en: Learn it inside the phrase economic prosperity, because the word is used most often about countries and regions.
normal.cn: 把它放在 economic prosperity 这个词组里记，因为它最常用来谈国家与地区。

abstract.en: Picture storehouses that are a little fuller each year: prosperity is the direction of the line, not a single good harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象一排粮仓，每年都比上一年满一点：繁荣是那条线的方向，而不是一次好收成。

abstract.en: A boom can end, so the word often takes a period word beside it, as in a decade of prosperity.
abstract.cn: 景气会结束，所以这个词旁边常带一个表示时间段的词，例如十年繁荣。

abstract.en: Shared prosperity asks whether the growth reaches ordinary tables, which is why the phrase carries moral weight.
abstract.cn: 共享繁荣问的是增长有没有落到普通人的餐桌上，这也是这个说法带有道德分量的原因。

examples.en: The new railway brought prosperity to villages that had been cut off for centuries.
examples.cn: 新铁路给那些与外界隔绝了几个世纪的村庄带来了繁荣。

examples.en: Economists still argue about how long the present prosperity can last.
examples.cn: 经济学家仍在争论当前的繁荣能持续多久。

examples.en: His prosperity began with a small workshop behind the family house.
examples.cn: 他的兴旺始于自家屋后的一间小作坊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「铺路拾贝提」：先把路铺好，再拾到贝壳，最后提到货，一路忙下来，家业就兴旺了。

root: 拉丁语 pro（向前）+ spes（希望）构成 prosperus（顺遂的、吉利的），其名词 prosperitas 经古法语 prosperite 进入英语。一般认为这一词源分析成立，但 prosperus 的具体构词仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hoped-for turn that really goes well; from that one idea grow economic boom, personal success, a dated period of good years, material comfort and the older sense of good fortune.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「盼来的转机真的变好」；由这一个念头长出经济繁荣、个人成功、可数的一段好年景、物质富足，以及较早的「好运、顺境」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: granaries filling up year after year while the ledger totals climb.
core.cn: 核心意象：粮仓一年比一年满，账本上的总数不断往上走。

branches.en: a harbour where loaded ships keep arriving and wages are paid on time
branches.cn: 货船不断进港、工钱按时发放的港口

branches.en: a man reading a good annual report at his desk
branches.cn: 一个人坐在桌前读一份漂亮的年报

branches.en: a stretch of good years marked on a timeline
branches.cn: 时间轴上被标出的一段好年头

branches.en: a warm house with a full table
branches.cn: 桌上摆满饭菜的暖屋子

branches.en: a New Year toast raised in a hall
branches.cn: 大厅里举起的祝酒

intro.en: Two Latin pieces, pro- and spes, plus a noun suffix explain how a hope becomes a verb, a state and a description.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁成分 pro- 与 spes，加上名词后缀，解释了「希望」如何变成动词、状态名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around spes is well recorded: a noun for hope, a verb for hoping, and the prosperus words for good fortune.
latinIntro.cn: spes 周围的拉丁词族有清楚记录：表示希望的名词、表示期盼的动词，以及表示好运的 prosperus 一族。

items.example: The small firm began to prosper.
items.exampleCN: 这家小公司开始兴旺起来。

definition_zh: 繁荣的；兴旺的；富裕的；成功的
definition_en: doing well and growing strong, especially in economic terms; wealthy and successful
core_image: 码头上吊塔不停转动，街边店铺的灯一直亮到深夜
scene: 铁路修通以后，原本安静的村子盖起了砖房，集市从清晨一直热闹到天黑。Within a decade the quiet village had become a prosperous trading town.
sceneCN: 这里 prosperous 是「繁荣的、兴旺的」（第 1 个义项：经济上有活力）；句意为十年之内，那个安静的村子变成了繁荣的贸易城镇。

pos.zh: 繁荣的；兴旺的；富裕的；成功的

derivatives.zh: prosperous 把 -ous 换成 -ity，得到「繁荣」这一状态名词
去掉后缀即得动词，意为「兴旺、发达」
prosperous 加 -ly 构成副词，意为「兴旺地、富足地」

senses.title: Economically strong and growing
senses.definition: having a strong economy, with growing trade, income and employment
senses.definitionCN: 经济强劲、贸易、收入与就业都在增长的
senses.example: The city grew prosperous on shipping and insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市靠航运与保险业繁荣起来。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the noun's outward signs but attaches them to a place: a town is prosperous when its cranes, ships and wages all point the same way.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了名词那套看得见的迹象，只是把它们贴到一个地方身上：吊塔、船只与工资都朝同一个方向走，这座城就是繁荣的。

senses.title: Making money; financially successful
senses.definition: doing well in business and earning a good income
senses.definitionCN: 生意做得顺、收入可观的
senses.example: She runs a prosperous little bakery near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站附近经营一家生意兴隆的小面包店。
senses.why: The suffix -ous turns the state into a quality, so the word can sit straight on a shop or a firm that keeps earning; growth is now read in takings rather than in the size of a region.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ous 把状态变成一种性质，于是这个词可以直接贴到一家持续赚钱的店铺或公司上；这时增长是从营业额里读出来的，而不是从地区规模里读出来的。

senses.title: Wealthy and comfortable
senses.definition: rich enough to live comfortably, especially of a person or a family
senses.definitionCN: 钱财足以过得舒适，尤指人或家庭
senses.example: Their prosperous neighbours lent them the money for the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们富裕的邻居借钱给他们修屋顶。
senses.why: Applied to people, the same quality shifts from output to comfort: what shows is not trade figures but a full table, warm rooms and the spare money that can be lent to a neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 用到人身上，同一种性质就从产出转向舒适：显出来的不是贸易数字，而是一桌饭菜、暖和的房间，以及能借给邻居的余钱。

senses.title: Successful and favourable; thriving
senses.definition: doing well or likely to do well; favourable, especially of a period or an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 走得顺或可望走顺的；有利的，尤指一段时间或一项事业
senses.example: The firm entered a prosperous season after the treaty was signed.
senses.exampleCN: 条约签订之后，这家公司进入了一段顺遂的时期。
senses.why: The oldest Latin layer meant favourable or lucky, and that colour returns when the word describes a period or a plan rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的拉丁义层是「顺遂的、吉利的」，当这个词形容一段时间或一个计划而不是一个地方时，那层意味就回来了。

intro.en: Prosperous is the Latin adjective prosperus, built on pro- 'forward' and spes 'hope', and it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: prosperous 就是拉丁形容词 prosperus，由 pro-「向前」与 spes「希望」构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Spes was the noun for hope, and the image behind it is a hope set in front of the eyes.
items.cn: spes 是表示希望的名词，背后的画面是把希望摆在眼前。

items.en: Pro- (forward) plus spes formed prosperus, meaning favourable or fortunate; this is the usual analysis, though the details are debated.
items.cn: pro-（向前）加 spes 构成 prosperus，意为顺遂的、吉利的；这是通常的分析，细节仍有争议。

items.en: The verb prosperare meant to thrive or to make something thrive, and it fed both the adjective and the noun.
items.cn: 动词 prosperare 意为兴旺、使兴旺，同时供养了形容词与名词。

items.en: Old French used prospere for fortunate and successful, and Middle English borrowed it in that shape.
items.cn: 古法语用 prospere 表示顺遂、成功，中古英语以这个形态借入。

items.en: Modern English prosperous describes economies, businesses, families and favourable periods, keeping the -ous adjective beside the -ity noun.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prosperous 可形容经济、企业、家庭与顺遂的时期，并让 -ous 结尾的形容词与 -ity 结尾的名词并排存在。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spes family and one near-spelling; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for wealth and healthy growth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spes 词族，并收一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示富裕与健康增长的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of doing well, formed with -ity where the adjective has -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的名词，形容词用 -ous 结尾，名词用 -ity 结尾。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to succeed and grow strong.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为兴旺、发达。

entries.definition: The adverb formed by adding -ly to this adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 本词加 -ly 构成的副词，意为兴旺地。

entries.definition: Only the spelling is close; this word means false and comes from Latin spurius, so the two are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，这个词意为虚假的，来自拉丁语 spurius，两者并无亲缘关系。

entries.definition: Growing strongly and doing well.
entries.definitionCN: 茁壮成长、势头很好的。

entries.definition: Having a lot of money and possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财与财物的。

entries.definition: Developing well and spreading strongly, often of plants, arts or business.
entries.definitionCN: 发展得好、势头旺盛的，常用于植物、艺术或生意。

entries.definition: Growing very fast, especially of trade or prices.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速增长的，尤指贸易或价格。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin adjective prosperus in English dress: pro- 'forward', spes 'hope', and the suffix -ous that makes a quality out of it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是换上英语外衣的拉丁形容词 prosperus：pro-「向前」、spes「希望」，以及把二者变成性质的 -ous。

normal.en: Pro- is forward, spes is hope, and -ous turns the pair into a quality, so prosperous describes something that hope has favoured.
normal.cn: pro- 是向前，spes 是希望，-ous 把这一对变成性质，所以 prosperous 形容被希望照顾到的事物。

normal.en: The noun twin is prosperity: -ous marks the adjective, -ity marks the noun, and the stem never changes.
normal.cn: 名词搭档是 prosperity：-ous 标记形容词，-ity 标记名词，词干始终不变。

normal.en: Prosper is the verb in the middle: prosperity and prosperous are both built on it, one as a state and one as a quality.
normal.cn: 中间的动词是 prosper：prosperity 与 prosperous 都建在它上面，一个表状态，一个表性质。

normal.en: Desperate shares the Latin hope word spes but adds de- 'without', so the two words pull in opposite directions.
normal.cn: desperate 共享拉丁语的希望 spes，但加上 de-「没有」，所以这两个词的方向正好相反。

normal.en: Note the spelling: the ending is -ous, not -ious, so there is no extra i before the u.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：结尾是 -ous 而不是 -ious，u 前面并没有多余的 i。

abstract.en: Think of a street where every second shutter is open and the lamps stay on late: that is prosperity seen as a quality.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，隔一家店就开着门，灯亮到很晚：这就是被看成一种性质的繁荣。

abstract.en: Add -ous and the word points at a thing; add -ity and it points at a condition. The suffix decides the grammar, not the meaning.
abstract.cn: 加 -ous，词就指向事物；加 -ity，词就指向状态。后缀决定语法角色，不决定意思。

abstract.en: A prosperous year and a year of prosperity say the same thing, one as a label and one as a period you can count.
abstract.cn: 「繁荣的一年」与「一段繁荣」说的是同一件事，一个像标签，一个像可以数出来的时间段。

examples.en: The city grew prosperous on shipping and insurance.
examples.cn: 这座城市靠航运与保险业繁荣起来。

examples.en: A prosperous town needs more than one good year.
examples.cn: 一座繁荣的城镇需要的远不止一个丰收年。

examples.en: They moved to a prosperous suburb with better schools.
examples.cn: 他们搬到了一个学校更好的富裕郊区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普罗斯珀勒斯」：先铺路，再拾珀，最后把家业勒紧攒起来，日子就兴旺了。

root: 拉丁语 pro（向前）+ spes（希望）构成 prosperus（顺遂的、吉利的），其动词 prosperare 意为兴旺；形容词经古法语 prospere 进入英语。一般认为词源分析成立，构词细节仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses keep the same picture of things going well; they differ only in where the success is read: a place, a business, a household, or a stretch of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项保留同一幅「事情顺利」的画面，区别只在于从哪里读出成功：一个地方、一门生意、一户人家，或一段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cranes turning over a busy dock while shop lights stay on late.
core.cn: 核心意象：繁忙码头上的吊塔不停转动，街边店铺的灯亮到深夜。

branches.en: a skyline of cranes above a working port
branches.cn: 工作港口上空的吊塔群

branches.en: a shop with a queue at the counter
branches.cn: 柜台前排着队的店铺

branches.en: a family eating in a warm dining room
branches.cn: 一家人在暖和的餐厅里吃饭

branches.en: a plan that keeps working out
branches.cn: 一步步走通的计划

branches.en: a town that stays lucky for years
branches.cn: 连续多年走运的城镇

intro.en: The stem is Latin; the two endings -ous and -ity do the English work of splitting quality from state.
intro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语；-ous 与 -ity 这两个结尾在英语里分工，一个表性质，一个表状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin recorded spes for hope, prosperus for fortunate, and prosperare for making something thrive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语留下了 spes（希望）、prosperus（顺遂的）与 prosperare（使兴旺）这几个形式。

items.exampleCN: 这门生意开始兴旺起来。
